# Exodus

שמות

Link: [https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus)

שעבוד בני ישראל במצרים, יציאת מצרים, מתן תורה ובניית המשכן.

The Israelites’ enslavement in Egypt, miraculous redemption, the giving of the Torah, and building of the Mishkan (Tabernacle).

Sections: Chapter-Verse

Location: Tanakh/Torah

Originally from [Sefaria](https://www.sefaria.org) via [TorahLM.org](https://torahlm.org) — see [licensing](https://torahlm.org/sefaria_license).

Version (He): Miqra according to the Masorah (Segments: 1210, License: CC-BY-SA)

Versions (En):
  - Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009 (Segments: 1210, License: CC-BY)
  - The Koren Jerusalem Bible (Segments: 1210, License: CC-BY-NC)
  - The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein (Segments: 1210, License: CC-BY)

וְאֵ֗לֶּה שְׁמוֹת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַבָּאִ֖ים מִצְרָ֑יְמָה אֵ֣ת יַעֲקֹ֔ב אִ֥ישׁ וּבֵית֖וֹ בָּֽאוּ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And these are the names of the children of Israel who came to Egypt, [Scripture mentioning them again, after their death, in G-d's love for them]; with Jacob, a man and his household they came.

Yissakhar, Zevulun, and Binyamin;

דָּ֥ן וְנַפְתָּלִ֖י גָּ֥ד וְאָשֵֽׁר׃

Don, Naftali, Gad and Asher.

Dan, Naftali, Gad, and Asher.

Dan, Naftali, Gad, and Asher.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:5)


וַֽיְהִ֗י כׇּל־נֶ֛פֶשׁ יֹצְאֵ֥י יֶֽרֶךְ־יַעֲקֹ֖ב שִׁבְעִ֣ים נָ֑פֶשׁ וְיוֹסֵ֖ף הָיָ֥ה בְמִצְרָֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
All the souls that emanated from the loins of Yaakov, [numbered] seventy souls, [including] Yoseif who was in Egypt.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And all the souls that came out of the loins of Ya῾aqov were seventy souls: for Yosef was already in Miżrayim.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

וַיָּ֤מׇת יוֹסֵף֙ וְכׇל־אֶחָ֔יו וְכֹ֖ל הַדּ֥וֹר הַהֽוּא׃

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:7)


וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל פָּר֧וּ וַֽיִּשְׁרְצ֛וּ וַיִּרְבּ֥וּ וַיַּֽעַצְמ֖וּ בִּמְאֹ֣ד מְאֹ֑ד וַתִּמָּלֵ֥א הָאָ֖רֶץ אֹתָֽם׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

And the children of Yisra᾽el were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and grew exceedingly mighty; and the land was filled with them.

And the children of Israel were fruitful, and teemed [six in one birth], and multiplied, and became exceedingly strong, and the land was filled with them.


###### Exodus 1:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:8)


וַיָּ֥קׇם מֶֽלֶךְ־חָדָ֖שׁ עַל־מִצְרָ֑יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־יָדַ֖ע אֶת־יוֹסֵֽף׃

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

###### Exodus 1:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:10)


הָ֥בָה נִֽתְחַכְּמָ֖ה ל֑וֹ פֶּן־יִרְבֶּ֗ה וְהָיָ֞ה כִּֽי־תִקְרֶ֤אנָה מִלְחָמָה֙ וְנוֹסַ֤ף גַּם־הוּא֙ עַל־שֹׂ֣נְאֵ֔ינוּ וְנִלְחַם־בָּ֖נוּ וְעָלָ֥ה מִן־הָאָֽרֶץ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Come let us deal wisely with him. Lest he increase so much, that, if there is war, he will join our enemies and fight against us, driving us from the land.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
come, let us deal wisely with them; lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when any war should chance, they also join our enemies, and fight against us, and so go up out of the land.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Ready yourselves to plot against it, lest it increase, and it shall be, in the event of war, that it, too, will be added to our foes, and it will war against us and go up out of the land.


###### Exodus 1:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:11)


וַיָּשִׂ֤ימוּ עָלָיו֙ שָׂרֵ֣י מִסִּ֔ים לְמַ֥עַן עַנֹּת֖וֹ בְּסִבְלֹתָ֑ם וַיִּ֜בֶן עָרֵ֤י מִסְכְּנוֹת֙ לְפַרְעֹ֔ה אֶת־פִּתֹ֖ם וְאֶת־רַעַמְסֵֽס׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
They appointed conscription officers over him to oppress him with their burdens. He [B’nei Yisrael] built supply cities for Pharaoh, Pisom and Ramseis.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Par῾o treasure cities, namely Pitom and Ra῾amses.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And they placed over it tax officers in order to afflict it with their [Egypt's] toils. And it built, [fortifying them as] treasure cities for Pharaoh — Pithom and Ramses.


###### Exodus 1:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:12)


וְכַאֲשֶׁר֙ יְעַנּ֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ כֵּ֥ן יִרְבֶּ֖ה וְכֵ֣ן יִפְרֹ֑ץ וַיָּקֻ֕צוּ מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
But the more [the Egyptians] oppressed him, the more [the B’nei Yisrael] increased and spread. [The Egyptians] came to loathe the B’nei Yisrael.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. And they were mortified on account of the children of Yisra᾽el.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And as [much as] they would afflict it, so did it multiply and so did it burst forth. And they were sick of their lives before the children of Israel.


###### Exodus 1:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:13)


וַיַּעֲבִ֧דוּ מִצְרַ֛יִם אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּפָֽרֶךְ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The Egyptians enslaved the B’nei Yisrael, with body-breaking labor.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And Miżrayim made the children of Yisra᾽el serve with rigour:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Egypt worked the children of Israel with (back-) breaking labor.


###### Exodus 1:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:14)


וַיְמָרְר֨וּ אֶת־חַיֵּיהֶ֜ם בַּעֲבֹדָ֣ה קָשָׁ֗ה בְּחֹ֙מֶר֙ וּבִלְבֵנִ֔ים וּבְכׇל־עֲבֹדָ֖ה בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה אֵ֚ת כׇּל־עֲבֹ֣דָתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־עָבְד֥וּ בָהֶ֖ם בְּפָֽרֶךְ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
They made their lives bitter with harsh labor involving mortar and bricks, and all kinds of work in the fields. All the work they made them do [was intended] to break them.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in mortar, and in brick, and in all manner of bondage in the field: all their bondage, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And they embittered their lives with hard toil: with mortar, and with brick, and with all the labor of the field; all of the labor with which they worked them was (back-) breaking.


###### Exodus 1:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:15)


וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם לַֽמְיַלְּדֹ֖ת הָֽעִבְרִיֹּ֑ת אֲשֶׁ֨ר שֵׁ֤ם הָֽאַחַת֙ שִׁפְרָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית פּוּעָֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives. The name of one of them was Shifrah, and the name of the other was Puah.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the king of Miżrayim spoke to the Hebrew midwives, of whom the name of the one was Shifra, and the name of the other Pu῾a:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, the name of the one, Shifrah [Yocheved, so called because she "beautifies" (meshapereth) the infant], and the name of the second, Puah [Miriam, so called because she "coos" (poah) to the infant].


###### Exodus 1:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:16)


וַיֹּ֗אמֶר בְּיַלֶּדְכֶן֙ אֶת־הָֽעִבְרִיּ֔וֹת וּרְאִיתֶ֖ן עַל־הָאׇבְנָ֑יִם אִם־בֵּ֥ן הוּא֙ וַהֲמִתֶּ֣ן אֹת֔וֹ וְאִם־בַּ֥ת הִ֖וא וָחָֽיָה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
He said, “When you deliver Hebrew women, you must look at the birthstool. If it is a boy, kill him; but if it is a girl, let her live.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and he said, When you do the office of midwife to the Hebrew women, you shall look upon the birth stones; if it be a son, then you shall kill him: but if it be a daughter, then she shall live.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And he said: When you deliver the Hebrew women, and you see upon the birth-stool that it is a son, then you shall kill him [(his astrologers having told him that a male would be born who would save Israel)], and if it is a daughter, then she shall live.


###### Exodus 1:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:17)


וַתִּירֶ֤אןָ הַֽמְיַלְּדֹת֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְלֹ֣א עָשׂ֔וּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ן מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרָ֑יִם וַתְּחַיֶּ֖יןָ אֶת־הַיְלָדִֽים׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The midwives [however] feared Elohim and did not do as the Egyptian king had told them, and they kept the infant boys alive.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Miżrayim commanded them, but saved the men children alive.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the midwives feared G-d and they did not do as the king of Egypt spoke to them, and they sustained the males.


###### Exodus 1:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:18)


וַיִּקְרָ֤א מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ לַֽמְיַלְּדֹ֔ת וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֔ן מַדּ֥וּעַ עֲשִׂיתֶ֖ן הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַתְּחַיֶּ֖יןָ אֶת־הַיְלָדִֽים׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The king of Egypt called for the midwives and said to them, “Why did you do this? You let the infant boys live.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the king of Miżrayim called for the midwives, and said to them, Why have you done this thing, and saved the men children alive?


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the king of Egypt called to the midwives and said to them: Why have you done this thing and sustained the males?


###### Exodus 1:19

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:19](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:19)


וַתֹּאמַ֤רְןָ הַֽמְיַלְּדֹת֙ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֔ה כִּ֣י לֹ֧א כַנָּשִׁ֛ים הַמִּצְרִיֹּ֖ת הָֽעִבְרִיֹּ֑ת כִּֽי־חָי֣וֹת הֵ֔נָּה בְּטֶ֨רֶם תָּב֧וֹא אֲלֵהֶ֛ן¹ הַמְיַלֶּ֖דֶת וְיָלָֽדוּ׃

footnotes:
¹ (בכתר ארם צובה היה כתוב אֲלֵיהֶ֛ן)


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The midwives said to Pharaoh, “The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptians. They know how to deliver. Even before a midwife gets to them, they have already given birth.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the midwives said to Par῾o, Because the Hebrew women are not as the Miżrian women; for they are lively, and are delivered before the midwives come to them.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the midwives said to Pharaoh: For not as the Egyptian women are the Hebrew women, for they are [as expert as] midwives. Before the midwives come to them, they are delivered [of themselves].


###### Exodus 1:20

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:20](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:20)


וַיֵּ֥יטֶב אֱלֹהִ֖ים לַֽמְיַלְּדֹ֑ת וַיִּ֧רֶב הָעָ֛ם וַיַּֽעַצְמ֖וּ מְאֹֽד׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Elohim was good to the midwives, and the people increased and were very mighty.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Therefore God dealt well with the midwives: and the people multiplied, and grew very mighty.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And G-d did good unto the midwives, and the people multiplied and grew very strong.


###### Exodus 1:21

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:21](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:21)


וַיְהִ֕י כִּֽי־יָרְא֥וּ הַֽמְיַלְּדֹ֖ת אֶת־הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיַּ֥עַשׂ לָהֶ֖ם בָּתִּֽים׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Because the midwives feared God, He gave them houses.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that he made them houses.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And it was, because the midwives feared G-d, that He made them houses [the houses of the Cohanim and the Levites from Yocheved, and the house of kingdom from Miriam (this being "the good" that He did unto them)].


###### Exodus 1:22

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:22](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/1:22)


וַיְצַ֣ו פַּרְעֹ֔ה לְכׇל־עַמּ֖וֹ לֵאמֹ֑ר כׇּל־הַבֵּ֣ן הַיִּלּ֗וֹד הַיְאֹ֙רָה֙ תַּשְׁלִיכֻ֔הוּ וְכׇל־הַבַּ֖ת תְּחַיּֽוּן׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Pharaoh then commanded all his people, saying, “Every boy who is born must be thrown into the river; but every girl shall be allowed to live.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And Par῾o charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born you shall cast into the River, and every daughter you shall save alive.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Pharaoh commanded his entire people, saying: Every son that is born, into the Nile shall you throw him, and every daughter shall you keep alive. [On the day of Moses' birth, Pharaoh's astrologers told him that the Jewish savior had been born and that he would be smitten by water, for which reason he decreed that all males be cast into the Nile — not knowing that Moses was destined to be "smitten" through the waters of Merivah (Numbers 20:13)].



## Chapter 2

###### Exodus 2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/2:1)


וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אִ֖ישׁ מִבֵּ֣ית לֵוִ֑י וַיִּקַּ֖ח אֶת־בַּת־לֵוִֽי׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
A man of the house of Levi went and married the daughter of Levi.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And there went a man from the house of Levi and took the daughter of Levi [after he had separated from her because of Pharaoh's decree (to drown the males)].

וַתַּ֥הַר הָאִשָּׁ֖ה וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַתֵּ֤רֶא אֹתוֹ֙ כִּי־ט֣וֹב ה֔וּא וַֽתִּצְפְּנֵ֖הוּ שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה יְרָחִֽים׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The woman conceived and bore a son. She saw that he was [exceptionally] good, and she kept him hidden for three months.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the woman conceived, and bore a son: and when she saw that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the woman conceived and bore a son, and she saw that he was good, [the house being filled with light at his birth], and she hid him for three months.


###### Exodus 2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/2:3)


וְלֹא־יָכְלָ֣ה עוֹד֮ הַצְּפִינוֹ֒ וַתִּֽקַּֽח־לוֹ֙ תֵּ֣בַת גֹּ֔מֶא וַתַּחְמְרָ֥הֿ בַחֵמָ֖ר וּבַזָּ֑פֶת וַתָּ֤שֶׂם בָּהּ֙ אֶת־הַיֶּ֔לֶד וַתָּ֥שֶׂם בַּסּ֖וּף עַל־שְׂפַ֥ת הַיְאֹֽר׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
When she could no longer hide him, she took a papyrus box and coated it with clay and tar. She placed the child in it, and placed it in the reeds near the bank of the river.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him a box made of papyrus, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child in it; and she laid it in the rushes by the River’s brink.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And she could conceal him no longer, and she took for him a reed casque [resistant to hard and soft], and she coated it with loam [on the inside] and with pitch [on the outside, so that "that tzaddik" not smell the foul odor of the pitch], and she put the child in it, and she placed it in the rushes by the banks of the Nile.

וַתִּפְתַּח֙ וַתִּרְאֵ֣הוּ אֶת־הַיֶּ֔לֶד וְהִנֵּה־נַ֖עַר בֹּכֶ֑ה וַתַּחְמֹ֣ל עָלָ֔יו וַתֹּ֕אמֶר מִיַּלְדֵ֥י הָֽעִבְרִ֖ים זֶֽה׃

###### Exodus 2:9

וַתֹּ֧אמֶר לָ֣הּ בַּת־פַּרְעֹ֗ה הֵילִ֜יכִי אֶת־הַיֶּ֤לֶד הַזֶּה֙ וְהֵינִקִ֣הוּ לִ֔י וַאֲנִ֖י אֶתֵּ֣ן אֶת־שְׂכָרֵ֑ךְ וַתִּקַּ֧ח הָאִשָּׁ֛ה הַיֶּ֖לֶד וַתְּנִיקֵֽהוּ׃

וַיִּ֤פֶן כֹּה֙ וָכֹ֔ה וַיַּ֖רְא כִּ֣י אֵ֣ין אִ֑ישׁ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת־הַמִּצְרִ֔י וַֽיִּטְמְנֵ֖הוּ בַּחֽוֹל׃

Elohim continued talking to Moshe, “This is what you must say to the B’nei Yisrael, ‘Adonoy, the God of your fathers, the God of Avraham, the God of Yitzchok, and the God of Yaakov, sent me to you. This is My eternal Name, and this is how I am to be mentioned for all generations.’”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

This [the Tetragrammaton] is My name forever (leolam) [written as "le'alem" ("to be concealed," i.e., not to be pronounced)], and this ["A-do-nai"] is My remembrance [i.e., pronunciation] from generation to generation.

###### Exodus 4:6

###### Exodus 4:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/4:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/4:7)


וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הָשֵׁ֤ב יָֽדְךָ֙ אֶל־חֵיקֶ֔ךָ וַיָּ֥שֶׁב יָד֖וֹ אֶל־חֵיק֑וֹ וַיּֽוֹצִאָהּ֙ מֵֽחֵיק֔וֹ וְהִנֵּה־שָׁ֖בָה כִּבְשָׂרֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And He said: Return your hand to your bosom, and he returned his hand to his bosom. And he took it from his bosom, and, behold, it had resumed its fleshy appearance, [whence it is derived that G-d's goodly measure is more expeditious than His punitive one ("from his bosom," as opposed to "took it out," above, implying that it had healed upon contact with his bosom)].


###### Exodus 4:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/4:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/4:8)


וְהָיָה֙ אִם־לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֣ינוּ לָ֔ךְ וְלֹ֣א יִשְׁמְע֔וּ לְקֹ֖ל הָאֹ֣ת הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן וְהֶֽאֱמִ֔ינוּ לְקֹ֖ל הָאֹ֥ת הָאַחֲרֽוֹן׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
“If they do not believe you, and they do not listen to the voice [of proof] of the first [miraculous] sign; then they will believe the voice [of proof] of the latter [second] sign.

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And it shall be, if they do not believe you, and they do not hearken to the message of the first sign, then they will believe the message of the last sign, [already having precedent (— as in the instance of Pharaoh and Avimelech, who were smitten with plague because of Sarah —) that the intenders of harm to them are smitten with plague.]

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

The sorcerers of Egypt did likewise with their magic art. Pharaoh’s heart remained hardened and he did not listen to them, just as Adonoy had spoken.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the magicians of Par῾o did so with their secret arts: and Par῾o’s heart was hardened, neither did he hearken to them; as the Lord had said.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the necromancers of Egypt did likewise through their charms. And Pharaoh's heart was strengthened and he did not pay heed to them, as the L-rd had spoken.


###### Exodus 7:23

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/7:23](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/7:23)


וַיִּ֣פֶן פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֖א אֶל־בֵּית֑וֹ וְלֹא־שָׁ֥ת לִבּ֖וֹ גַּם־לָזֹֽאת׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Pharaoh turned and went into his house, and paid no attention even to this [miracle].


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And Par῾o turned and went to his house, neither did he set his heart even to this.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Pharaoh turned and came to his house, and he did not set his heart to this [the plague of blood], too, [as well as (not) to the staff's turning into a serpent].


###### Exodus 7:24

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/7:24](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/7:24)


וַיַּחְפְּר֧וּ כׇל־מִצְרַ֛יִם סְבִיבֹ֥ת הַיְאֹ֖ר מַ֣יִם לִשְׁתּ֑וֹת כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָֽכְלוּ֙ לִשְׁתֹּ֔ת מִמֵּימֵ֖י הַיְאֹֽר׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The Egyptians dug around the river for water to drink, for they could not drink from the waters of the river.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And all Miżrayim dug round about the River for water to drink; for they could not drink of the water of the River.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And all of Egypt dug around the Nile for water to drink, for they could not drink from the waters of the Nile.


###### Exodus 7:25

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/7:25](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/7:25)


וַיִּמָּלֵ֖א שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים אַחֲרֵ֥י הַכּוֹת־יְהֹוָ֖ה אֶת־הַיְאֹֽר׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Seven full days [passed] after Adonoy had struck the river.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And seven days were completed, after the Lord had smitten the River.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And seven days [of plague] were completed after the L-rd had smitten the Nile [before it returned to its original state, each plague obtaining for a quarter of a month, and three-quarters for warning.]


###### Exodus 7:26

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/7:26](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/7:26)


וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה בֹּ֖א אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהֹוָ֔ה שַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־עַמִּ֖י וְיַֽעַבְדֻֽנִי׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Adonoy said to Moshe, “Go to Pharaoh and say to him, ‘This is what Adonoy has said, “Send out my people so they may worship Me.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the Lord spoke to Moshe, Go to Par῾o, and say to him, Thus says the Lord, Let my people go, that they may serve me.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the L-rd said to Moses: Come to Pharaoh and say to him: Thus said the L-rd: Send out My people and let them serve Me.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/7:27](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/7:27)


וְאִם־מָאֵ֥ן אַתָּ֖ה לְשַׁלֵּ֑חַ הִנֵּ֣ה אָנֹכִ֗י נֹגֵ֛ף אֶת־כׇּל־גְּבוּלְךָ֖ בַּֽצְפַרְדְּעִֽים׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If you refuse to send [them,] behold I will plague all your borders [territories] with frogs.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And if thou refuse to let them go, behold, I will smite all thy borders with frogs:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if you are a refuser, (not) to send out, behold, I shall smite all of your border with frogs.


###### Exodus 7:28

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/7:28](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/7:28)


וְשָׁרַ֣ץ הַיְאֹר֮ צְפַרְדְּעִים֒ וְעָלוּ֙ וּבָ֣אוּ בְּבֵיתֶ֔ךָ וּבַחֲדַ֥ר מִשְׁכָּבְךָ֖ וְעַל־מִטָּתֶ֑ךָ וּבְבֵ֤ית עֲבָדֶ֙יךָ֙ וּבְעַמֶּ֔ךָ וּבְתַנּוּרֶ֖יךָ וּבְמִשְׁאֲרוֹתֶֽיךָ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The river will swarm with frogs. They will emerge and come into your house, into your bedroom, and on your bed, into the houses of your servants and your people, into your ovens and into your kneading bowls.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and the river shall bring forth frogs in swarms, and these will go up and come into thy house, and into thy bedchamber, and upon thy bed, and into the house of thy servants, and upon thy people, and into thy ovens, and into thy kneading troughs:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the Nile shall swarm frogs, and they shall go up [from the Nile] and come [first] into your house, [Pharaoh having counseled first against the Jews (1:9)], and into your bed chamber and upon your bed, and [then] into the house of your servants, and into your people, and into your ovens and into your kneading troughs.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/7:29](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/7:29)

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Upon you and upon your people and upon all your servants the frogs will emerge.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and the frogs shall come up both on thee, and on thy people, and on all thy servants.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And in you [i.e., in your innards] and in your people and in all of your servants shall the frogs go up.



## Chapter 8

###### Exodus 8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/8:1)


וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהֹוָה֮ אֶל־מֹשֶׁה֒ אֱמֹ֣ר אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֗ן נְטֵ֤ה אֶת־יָדְךָ֙ בְּמַטֶּ֔ךָ עַ֨ל־הַנְּהָרֹ֔ת עַל־הַיְאֹרִ֖ים וְעַל־הָאֲגַמִּ֑ים וְהַ֥עַל אֶת־הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִ֖ים עַל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Adonoy said to Moshe, “Say to Aharon, ‘Extend your hand with your rod over the rivers, over the streams and over the lakes, and bring up the frogs upon the land of Egypt.’”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the Lord spoke to Moshe, Say to Aharon, Stretch forth thy hand with thy rod over the streams, over the canals, and over the ponds, and cause frogs to come up upon the land of Miżrayim.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the L-rd said to Moses: Say to Aaron: Stretch your hand with the staff over the rivers, over the water courses, and over the ponds, and bring up the frogs upon the land of Egypt.


###### Exodus 8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/8:2)


וַיֵּ֤ט אַהֲרֹן֙ אֶת־יָד֔וֹ עַ֖ל מֵימֵ֣י מִצְרָ֑יִם וַתַּ֙עַל֙ הַצְּפַרְדֵּ֔עַ וַתְּכַ֖ס אֶת־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Aharon extended his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frog emerged and covered the land of Egypt.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And Aharon stretched out his hand over the waters of Miżrayim. And the frogs came up, and covered the land of Miżrayim.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Aaron stretched forth his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frog [swarm] came up and covered the land of Egypt.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/8:3)


וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־כֵ֥ן הַֽחַרְטֻמִּ֖ים בְּלָטֵיהֶ֑ם וַיַּעֲל֥וּ אֶת־הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִ֖ים עַל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The sorcerers did likewise with their magic art, and made the frogs emerge upon the land of Egypt.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the necromancers did likewise through their charms, and the frogs came up upon the land of Egypt.


###### Exodus 8:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/8:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/8:4)


וַיִּקְרָ֨א פַרְעֹ֜ה לְמֹשֶׁ֣ה וּֽלְאַהֲרֹ֗ן וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הַעְתִּ֣ירוּ אֶל־יְהֹוָ֔ה וְיָסֵר֙ הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִ֔ים מִמֶּ֖נִּי וּמֵֽעַמִּ֑י וַאֲשַׁלְּחָה֙ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם וְיִזְבְּח֖וּ לַיהֹוָֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Pharaoh called for Moshe and Aharon and said, “Pray to Adonoy, and let Him remove the frogs from me and from my people, and I will send the people to sacrifice to Adonoy.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Then Par῾o called to Moshe and Aharon, and said, Entreat the Lord, that he may take away the frogs from me, and from my people; and I will let the people go, that they may do sacrifice to the Lord.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Pharaoh called to Moses and to Aaron and he said: Entreat the L-rd that he remove the frogs from me and from my people, and I will send out the people and they will sacrifice to the L-rd.


###### Exodus 8:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/8:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/8:5)


וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֣ה לְפַרְעֹה֮ הִתְפָּאֵ֣ר עָלַי֒ לְמָתַ֣י**׀** אַעְתִּ֣יר לְךָ֗ וְלַעֲבָדֶ֙יךָ֙ וּֽלְעַמְּךָ֔ לְהַכְרִית֙ הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִ֔ים מִמְּךָ֖ וּמִבָּתֶּ֑יךָ רַ֥ק בַּיְאֹ֖ר תִּשָּׁאַֽרְנָה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Moshe said to Pharaoh, “Glorify yourself at my expense. [Exactly for] when shall I pray for you, and for your servants and for your people, that the frogs be destroyed from you and from your houses, remaining only in the river.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And Moshe said to Par῾o, Challenge me to fix a time when I should entreat for thee, and for thy servants, and for thy people, to destroy the frogs from thee and thy houses, that they may remain in the River only?


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Moses said to Pharaoh: "Presume" over me as to when I should entreat for you and for your servants and for your people to cut off the frogs from you and from your houses. Only in the Nile shall they remain.


###### Exodus 8:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/8:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/8:6)


וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לְמָחָ֑ר וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ כִּדְבָ֣רְךָ֔ לְמַ֣עַן תֵּדַ֔ע כִּי־אֵ֖ין כַּיהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
[Pharaoh] said, “By tomorrow.” [Moshe] said, “As you say. You will then know that there is none like Adonoy, our God.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And he said, Tomorrow. And he said, Be it according to thy word: that thou mayst know that there is none like the Lord our God.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And he said: [Entreat today] for tomorrow [i.e., that they be cut off tomorrow]. And he said: As you say. So that you know that there is none like the L-rd our G-d.


###### Exodus 8:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/8:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/8:7)


וְסָר֣וּ הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִ֗ים מִמְּךָ֙ וּמִבָּ֣תֶּ֔יךָ וּמֵעֲבָדֶ֖יךָ וּמֵעַמֶּ֑ךָ רַ֥ק בַּיְאֹ֖ר תִּשָּׁאַֽרְנָה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The frogs will be removed from you, from your houses, from your servants and from your people. They will remain only in the river.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the frogs shall depart from thee, and from thy houses, and from thy servants, and from thy people; they shall remain in the River only.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the frogs will depart from you and from your houses and from your servants and from your people; only in the Nile shall they remain.


###### Exodus 8:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/8:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/8:8)


וַיֵּצֵ֥א מֹשֶׁ֛ה וְאַהֲרֹ֖ן מֵעִ֣ם פַּרְעֹ֑ה וַיִּצְעַ֤ק מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־יְהֹוָ֔ה עַל־דְּבַ֥ר הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִ֖ים אֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֥ם לְפַרְעֹֽה׃

וַיַּ֥עַשׂ יְהֹוָ֖ה כִּדְבַ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיָּמֻ֙תוּ֙ הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִ֔ים מִן־הַבָּתִּ֥ים מִן־הַחֲצֵרֹ֖ת וּמִן־הַשָּׂדֹֽת׃

Adonoy did as Moshe said, the frogs died, [those that were in] the houses, the courtyards, and the fields.

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the L-rd did according to the word of Moses and the frogs died out of the houses, out of the courtyards, and out of the fields.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/8:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/8:10)


וַיִּצְבְּר֥וּ אֹתָ֖ם חֳמָרִ֣ם חֳמָרִ֑ם וַתִּבְאַ֖שׁ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

They gathered them into [many] heaps, and the land was polluted.

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
[When] Pharaoh saw that there was respite, he hardened his heart and did not listen to them, just as Adonoy had spoken.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

###### Exodus 8:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/8:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/8:12)


וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהֹוָה֮ אֶל־מֹשֶׁה֒ אֱמֹר֙ אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֔ן נְטֵ֣ה אֶֽת־מַטְּךָ֔ וְהַ֖ךְ אֶת־עֲפַ֣ר הָאָ֑רֶץ וְהָיָ֥ה לְכִנִּ֖ם בְּכׇל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Adonoy said to Moshe, “Say to Aharon, Extend your rod and strike the dust of the earth; and it will turn into lice throughout the whole land of Egypt.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the Lord said to Moshe, Say to Aharon, Stretch out thy rod, and smite the dust of the land, that it may turn into lice throughout all the land of Miżrayim.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the L-rd said to Moses: Say to Aaron: Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the earth [(It was not fitting that the earth be struck by Moses, for it had "protected" him when he had killed the Egyptian, for which reason Aaron was bidden to strike it)], and it will be lice in all the land of Egypt.


###### Exodus 8:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/8:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/8:13)


וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־כֵ֗ן וַיֵּט֩ אַהֲרֹ֨ן אֶת־יָד֤וֹ בְמַטֵּ֙הוּ֙ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת־עֲפַ֣ר הָאָ֔רֶץ וַתְּהִי֙ הַכִּנָּ֔ם בָּאָדָ֖ם וּבַבְּהֵמָ֑ה כׇּל־עֲפַ֥ר הָאָ֛רֶץ הָיָ֥ה כִנִּ֖ים בְּכׇל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

and if the household be too little for a lamb, let him and his neighbour next to his house take it according to the number of the souls; according to every man’s eating shall you make your count for the lamb.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if the household is too small for one lamb [so that some of it would be left over (nothar, which is forbidden)], then he and his neighbor next to his house shall take it according to the count of souls. Each according to his eating [(excluding one who is so sick or old that he cannot eat at least an olive size)] shall you [include in the] count for the lamb.

A flawless lamb, a yearling male must be in your possession. You may take it from sheep or goats.

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

and you shall keep it until the fourteenth day of the same month: and the whole assembly of the congregation of Yisra᾽el shall kill it towards evening.

###### Exodus 12:18

בָּרִאשֹׁ֡ן בְּאַרְבָּעָה֩ עָשָׂ֨ר י֤וֹם לַחֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ בָּעֶ֔רֶב תֹּאכְל֖וּ מַצֹּ֑ת עַ֠ד י֣וֹם הָאֶחָ֧ד וְעֶשְׂרִ֛ים לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ בָּעָֽרֶב׃

###### Exodus 12:19

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:19](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:19)

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
For seven days leaven may not be found in your homes, for whoever eats chametz that soul shall be cut off from the community of Israel, whether a proselyte or a native born in the land.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Seven days shall there be no leaven found in your houses: for whoever eats that which is leavened, even that soul shall be cut off from the congregation of Yisra᾽el, whether he be a stranger, or born in the land.

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You must not eat anything that is chametz. In all your dwellings you shall eat matzos.

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

וּמוֹשַׁב֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָשְׁב֖וּ בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וְאַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The habitation of the B’nei Yisrael living in Egypt lasted four hundred and thirty years.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Now the sojourning of the children of Yisra᾽el, who dwelt in Miżrayim, was four hundred and thirty years.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the habitation of the children of Israel in the land of Egypt [and their habitations outside it after "Your seed shall be a stranger, etc." (Genesis 15:13)] was [all together] four hundred and thirty years.


###### Exodus 12:41

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:41](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:41)


וַיְהִ֗י מִקֵּץ֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וְאַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה וַיְהִ֗י בְּעֶ֙צֶם֙ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה יָ֥צְא֛וּ כׇּל־צִבְא֥וֹת יְהֹוָ֖ה מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
It was at the end of the four hundred and thirty years, and on that very day all of Adonoy’s multitudes went out of the land of Egypt.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And it came to pass at the end of four hundred and thirty years, even on that very day it came to pass, that all the hosts of the Lord went out from the land of Miżrayim.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And it was at the end of four hundred and thirty years, and it was on this very same day [the fifteenth of Nissan, (the date of the angels' tidings to Abraham on the birth of a son, the date of Isaac's birth, the date of the covenant between the pieces — the L-rd not delaying an instant after the arrival of the foretold time)] that all the hosts of the L-rd went out of the land of Egypt.


###### Exodus 12:42

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:42](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:42)


לֵ֣יל שִׁמֻּרִ֥ים הוּא֙ לַֽיהֹוָ֔ה לְהוֹצִיאָ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם הֽוּא־הַלַּ֤יְלָה הַזֶּה֙ לַֽיהֹוָ֔ה שִׁמֻּרִ֛ים לְכׇל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְדֹרֹתָֽם׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
This was a night of vigil for Adonoy, to bring them out of the land of Egypt. This night remains a night of vigil to Adonoy for all the B’nei Yisrael for [all] their generations.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
It is a night of watchfulness to the Lord for bringing them out from the land of Miżrayim: this is the Lord’s watchnight, for all the children of Yisra᾽el in their generations.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
It is a night of guarding for the L-rd, ["guarded" by the L-rd] to take them out from the land of Egypt; it is "this night" of the L-rd [i.e., of His saying to Abraham: "On this night I shall redeem your children"], guarded [against destructive agents] for all the children of Israel for (all) their generations [see 33].


###### Exodus 12:43

וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאַהֲרֹ֔ן זֹ֖את חֻקַּ֣ת הַפָּ֑סַח כׇּל־בֶּן־נֵכָ֖ר לֹא־יֹ֥אכַל בּֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Adonoy said to Moshe and Aharon, “This is the statute of the Pesach offering: No alien may eat it.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the Lord said to Moshe and Aharon, This is the ordinance of the passover: no stranger shall eat of it:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the L-rd said to Moses and Aaron [(on the fourteenth of Nissan)]: This is the statute of the paschal offering: No stranger [(Both a heretical Jew and a non-Jew are implied)] may eat of it.


###### Exodus 12:44

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:44](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:44)


וְכׇל־עֶ֥בֶד אִ֖ישׁ מִקְנַת־כָּ֑סֶף וּמַלְתָּ֣ה אֹת֔וֹ אָ֖ז יֹ֥אכַל בּֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
However each man’s slave [if he was]purchased with money, you must circumcise him and then he may eat it.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
but every man’s servant that is bought for money, when thou hast circumcised him, then shall he eat of it.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And every man-servant acquired by money — you shall circumcise him; then shall he [(according to one view, the master; according to another, the servant)] eat of it.


###### Exodus 12:45

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:45](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:45)


תּוֹשָׁ֥ב וְשָׂכִ֖יר לֹא־יֹ֥אכַל בּֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
An [alien] sojourner or hired worker may not eat it.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
A foreigner and a hired servant shall not eat of it.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
A sojourner [a ger toshav (one who does not convert fully, but who undertakes not to serve idols and to observe the seven Noahide laws)] and a hired man [a non-Jew] may not eat of it. [The above applies (even) to a circumcised Arab or a circumcised Giveonite who is a sojourner or a hired man.]


###### Exodus 12:46

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:46](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:46)


בְּבַ֤יִת אֶחָד֙ יֵאָכֵ֔ל לֹא־תוֹצִ֧יא מִן־הַבַּ֛יִת מִן־הַבָּשָׂ֖ר ח֑וּצָה וְעֶ֖צֶם לֹ֥א תִשְׁבְּרוּ־בֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
It must be eaten in one house. You must not remove from the house any of its flesh, to the outdoors, and you must not break any of its bones.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
In one house shall it be eaten: thou shalt not take any of the meat outside, out of the house; neither shall you break a bone of it.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
In one house [i.e., group] shall it be eaten. Do not take from the house [i.e., from the group] of the flesh outside. And a bone [which has an olive-size of meat on it] shall you not break in it.


###### Exodus 12:47

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:47](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:47)


כׇּל־עֲדַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יַעֲשׂ֥וּ אֹתֽוֹ׃

The entire community of Yisrael must make this [offering].


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
All the congregation of Yisra᾽el shall keep it.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The entire congregation of Israel [in any groups] shall offer it [in future generations, (as opposed to the Pesach of Egypt, when it was offered by family groups)].


###### Exodus 12:48

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:48](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:48)


וְכִֽי־יָג֨וּר אִתְּךָ֜ גֵּ֗ר וְעָ֣שָׂה פֶ֘סַח֮ לַיהֹוָה֒ הִמּ֧וֹל ל֣וֹ כׇל־זָכָ֗ר וְאָז֙ יִקְרַ֣ב לַעֲשֹׂת֔וֹ וְהָיָ֖ה כְּאֶזְרַ֣ח הָאָ֑רֶץ וְכׇל־עָרֵ֖ל לֹֽא־יֹ֥אכַל בּֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
When a proselyte dwells with you and wants to make the Pesach-offering to Adonoy, every male must be circumcised. He may then come near [join] to make it, and be like the native born. But no uncircumcised male may eat of it.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And when a stranger shall sojourn with thee, and will keep the passover to the Lord, let all his males be circumcised, and then let him come near and keep it; and he shall be as one that is born in the land: for no uncircumcised person shall eat of it.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if there live with you a stranger (i.e., a proselyte) and he would offer a paschal offering to the L-rd [on the fourteenth of Nissan], let all of his males be circumcised and then he shall draw near to offer it. And he shall be as the citizen of the land, and no uncircumcised one shall eat of it [(including one who is not circumcised because his brothers have died as a result of circumcision)].


###### Exodus 12:49

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:49](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:49)


תּוֹרָ֣ה אַחַ֔ת יִהְיֶ֖ה לָֽאֶזְרָ֑ח וְלַגֵּ֖ר הַגָּ֥ר בְּתוֹכְכֶֽם׃

There shall be one law for the native born and for the proselyte who dwells among you.

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:50](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/12:50)


וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֖וּ כׇּל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהֹוָ֛ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאֶֽת־אַהֲרֹ֖ן כֵּ֥ן עָשֽׂוּ׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
All the B’nei Yisrael did as Adonoy commanded Moshe and Aharon. They [Moshe and Aharon] also did so.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thus did all the children of Yisra᾽el; as the Lord commanded Moshe and Aharon so they did.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
On that very day, Adonoy took the B’nei Yisrael out of Egypt in their multitudes.

קַדֶּשׁ־לִ֨י כׇל־בְּכ֜וֹר פֶּ֤טֶר כׇּל־רֶ֙חֶם֙ בִּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בָּאָדָ֖ם וּבַבְּהֵמָ֑ה לִ֖י הֽוּא׃

“Sanctify to Me all the first-born, that [is the first to] open the womb among the B’nei Yisrael, both of man and beast, it is Mine.”

###### Exodus 13:3

וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶל־הָעָ֗ם זָכ֞וֹר אֶת־הַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְצָאתֶ֤ם מִמִּצְרַ֙יִם֙ מִבֵּ֣ית עֲבָדִ֔ים כִּ֚י בְּחֹ֣זֶק יָ֔ד הוֹצִ֧יא יְהֹוָ֛ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִזֶּ֑ה וְלֹ֥א יֵאָכֵ֖ל חָמֵֽץ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Moshe said to the people, “Remember this day [as the day] on which you came out of Egypt, from the house of slavery, for with a strong hand Adonoy brought you out from this. You must not eat chametz.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And Moshe said to the people, Remember this day, in which you came out from Miżrayim, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand the Lord brought you out from this place: no leavened bread shall be eaten.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Moses said to the people: Remember this day when you went out of Egypt from the house of bondage [(We are hereby taught to make mention of the exodus every day)]. For with might of hand did the L-rd take you hence, and chametz shall not be eaten.


###### Exodus 13:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/13:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/13:4)


הַיּ֖וֹם אַתֶּ֣ם יֹצְאִ֑ים בְּחֹ֖דֶשׁ הָאָבִֽיב׃

**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
This day you came out, in the month Aviv.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
This day you go out, in the month of spring [an equable month: neither hot, nor cold, nor rainy.]


###### Exodus 13:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/13:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/13:5)


וְהָיָ֣ה כִֽי־יְבִיאֲךָ֣ יְהֹוָ֡ה אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ הַֽ֠כְּנַעֲנִ֠י וְהַחִתִּ֨י וְהָאֱמֹרִ֜י וְהַחִוִּ֣י וְהַיְבוּסִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֤ע לַאֲבֹתֶ֙יךָ֙ לָ֣תֶת לָ֔ךְ אֶ֛רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָ֑שׁ וְעָבַדְתָּ֛ אֶת־הָעֲבֹדָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַזֶּֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
When Adonoy brings you to the land of the Canaanite, the Chittites, the Emorites, the Chivites and the Yevusites, which He swore to your fathers [that He would] give to you—a land flowing with milk and honey—you must conduct this service in this month.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And it shall be when the Lord shall bring thee into the land of the Kena῾ani, and the Ḥitti, and the Emori, and the Ḥivvi, and the Yevusi, which he swore to thy fathers to give thee, a land flowing with milk and honey, that thou shalt keep this service in this month.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And it shall be, when the L-rd brings you to the land of Canaan [(a particular nation of the seven nations generically called "Canaanites")], the Chitti, the Emori, the Chivi, and the Yevussi, which He swore to your forefathers to give to you [(Abraham — Genesis 15:18; Isaac — 26:3; Jacob — 28:13)], a land flowing with milk [from goats] and honey [from dates and figs], then you shall perform this service [of Pesach] on this month.


###### Exodus 13:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/13:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/13:6)


שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים תֹּאכַ֣ל מַצֹּ֑ת וּבַיּוֹם֙ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י חַ֖ג לַיהֹוָֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
For seven days you must eat matzos, and the seventh day is a festival to Adonoy.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Seven days thou shalt eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a feast to the Lord.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Seven days shall you eat matzoth, and on the seventh day, a festival to the L-rd.


###### Exodus 13:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/13:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/13:7)


מַצּוֹת֙ יֵֽאָכֵ֔ל אֵ֖ת שִׁבְעַ֣ת הַיָּמִ֑ים וְלֹֽא־יֵרָאֶ֨ה לְךָ֜ חָמֵ֗ץ וְלֹֽא־יֵרָאֶ֥ה לְךָ֛ שְׂאֹ֖ר בְּכׇל־גְּבֻלֶֽךָ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Matzos must be eaten these seven days. No chametz may be seen in your possession, and no leaven may be seen in all your boundaries.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Matzoth shall be eaten the seven days; and chametz (leaven) shall not be seen unto you, and se'or (leavening) shall not be seen unto you in all of your boundaries.


###### Exodus 13:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/13:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/13:8)


וְהִגַּדְתָּ֣ לְבִנְךָ֔ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא לֵאמֹ֑ר בַּעֲב֣וּר זֶ֗ה עָשָׂ֤ה יְהֹוָה֙ לִ֔י בְּצֵאתִ֖י מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You must tell your son [child] on that day saying, ‘Because of this, Adonoy did [this] for me when I came out of Egypt.’


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt relate to thy son on that day, saying, This is done because of that which the Lord did to me when I came out of Miżrayim.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall tell [vehigadeta] your son [(an allusion to "the son who does not know how to ask." "Open for him" with words of aggadah (narration), which stimulate questioning)] on that day, saying: Because of this [i.e., so that I fulfill His mitzvoth, e.g., pesach, matzoth, and maror] the L-rd wrought for me when I went out of Egypt [(an allusion to the answer to "the wicked son," (see 12:26), viz.: "The L-rd wrought for me and not for you. Had you been there, you would not have merited redemption.")]


###### Exodus 13:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/13:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/13:9)


וְהָיָה֩ לְךָ֨ לְא֜וֹת עַל־יָדְךָ֗ וּלְזִכָּרוֹן֙ בֵּ֣ין עֵינֶ֔יךָ לְמַ֗עַן תִּהְיֶ֛ה תּוֹרַ֥ת יְהֹוָ֖ה בְּפִ֑יךָ כִּ֚י בְּיָ֣ד חֲזָקָ֔ה הוֹצִֽאֲךָ֥ יְהֹוָ֖ה מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

###### Exodus 14:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/14:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/14:4)

###### Exodus 14:5

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם ה֚וּא אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהֹוָ֔ה שַׁבָּת֧וֹן שַׁבַּת־קֹ֛דֶשׁ לַֽיהֹוָ֖ה מָחָ֑ר אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־תֹּאפ֞וּ אֵפ֗וּ וְאֵ֤ת אֲשֶֽׁר־תְּבַשְּׁלוּ֙ בַּשֵּׁ֔לוּ וְאֵת֙ כׇּל־הָ֣עֹדֵ֔ף הַנִּ֧יחוּ לָכֶ֛ם לְמִשְׁמֶ֖רֶת עַד־הַבֹּֽקֶר׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
He said to them, “This is what Adonoy has said: Tomorrow is a [day of] rest, Adonoy’s holy Shabbos. Bake what you want to bake, and cook what you want to cook, and whatever is left over, put aside for yourselves, to preserve it until the morning.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And he said to them, This is that which the Lord has said, Tomorrow is the rest of the holy sabbath to the Lord: bake that which you will bake today, and what you will boil, boil today; and that which remains over lay up for you to be kept until the morning.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And he said to them: This is what the L-rd had spoken: A resting, a holy Sabbath is it to the L-rd tomorrow. What you bake [in an oven] (of the manna)] bake [all of it today for two days], and what you would cook [in water] cook; and all the rest put by for yourselves in keeping until the morning.

They put it aside until morning as Moshe had commanded. It did not turn putrid and there were no worms in it.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And they put it by until the morning, as the L-rd had commanded Moses, and it did not rot, and there was no worm in it.

וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אִכְלֻ֣הוּ הַיּ֔וֹם כִּֽי־שַׁבָּ֥ת הַיּ֖וֹם לַיהֹוָ֑ה הַיּ֕וֹם לֹ֥א תִמְצָאֻ֖הוּ בַּשָּׂדֶֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Moshe said, “Eat it today, for today is Shabbos to Adonoy. Today you will not find it [manna] in the field.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
[In the morning, when they were wont to go out and gather the manna, they came and asked Moses: "Shall we go out or not?"] And Moses said: Eat it [(what you have)] today. [They returned towards evening and asked: "Shall we go out now?" He answered that they should not] for it is Sabbath today to the L-rd. [Seeing them to be worried that the manna might not fall again, he said:] Today you will not find it in the field, [but tomorrow you will.]

###### Exodus 16:29

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/16:29](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/16:29)


רְא֗וּ כִּֽי־יְהֹוָה֮ נָתַ֣ן לָכֶ֣ם הַשַּׁבָּת֒ עַל־כֵּ֠ן ה֣וּא נֹתֵ֥ן לָכֶ֛ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁ֖י לֶ֣חֶם יוֹמָ֑יִם שְׁב֣וּ**׀** אִ֣ישׁ תַּחְתָּ֗יו אַל־יֵ֥צֵא אִ֛ישׁ מִמְּקֹמ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִֽי׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
See, because Adonoy gave you the Shabbos, therefore He gave you on the sixth day bread for two days. Every man must remain in his place. No man may go out of his place on the seventh day.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
See, that the Lord has given you the sabbath, therefore he gives you on the sixth day the bread of two days: remain every man in his place, let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
See [with your own eyes] that the L-rd has given you the Sabbath [to be observed], wherefore He gives you on the sixth day bread for two days. Let each man sit in his place; let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.

###### Exodus 16:35

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/16:35](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/16:35)


וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אָֽכְל֤וּ אֶת־הַמָּן֙ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה עַד־בֹּאָ֖ם אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ נוֹשָׁ֑בֶת אֶת־הַמָּן֙ אָֽכְל֔וּ עַד־בֹּאָ֕ם אֶל־קְצֵ֖ה אֶ֥רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The B’nei Yisrael ate the manna for forty years, until they came to an inhabited land. They ate the manna until they came to the edge of the land of Canaan.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the children of Israel ate the manna for forty years until they came to an inhabited land [on the other side of the Jordan (see Joshua 5:11-12)]. They had eaten the manna [that had fallen on the seventh of Adar, (when Moses died, the manna ceasing with his death)], until they came to the edge of the land of Canaan [before they crossed the Jordan].

## Chapter 17

###### Exodus 17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/17:1)


וַ֠יִּסְע֠וּ כׇּל־עֲדַ֨ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל מִמִּדְבַּר־סִ֛ין לְמַסְעֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־פִּ֣י יְהֹוָ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנוּ֙ בִּרְפִידִ֔ים וְאֵ֥ין מַ֖יִם לִשְׁתֹּ֥ת הָעָֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The entire community of B’nei Yisrael journeyed from the wilderness of Sin, traveling according to the word of Adonoy. They camped in Rephidim, and there was no water for the people to drink.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And all the congregation of the children of Yisra᾽el journeyed from the wilderness of Sin, by their stages, according to the commandment of the Lord, and pitched in Refidim: and there was no water for the people to drink.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the entire congregation of the children of Israel journeyed from the desert of Sin in their journeys by the word of the L-rd, and they encamped in Refidim; and there was no water to drink for the people.


###### Exodus 17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/17:2)


וַיָּ֤רֶב הָעָם֙ עִם־מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ תְּנוּ־לָ֥נוּ מַ֖יִם וְנִשְׁתֶּ֑ה וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה מַה־תְּרִיבוּן֙ עִמָּדִ֔י מַה־תְּנַסּ֖וּן אֶת־יְהֹוָֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The people quarreled with Moshe, and said, “Give us water to drink.” Moshe said to them, “Why are you quarreling with me? Why are you testing Adonoy?”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Wherefore the people did strive with Moshe, and said, Give us water that we may drink. And Moshe said to them, Why do you strive with me? why do you tempt the Lord?


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the people quarreled with Moses, and they said: Give us water and let us drink. And Moses said to them: Why would you quarrel with me? Why would you try the L-rd [to see if He can give water in a dry land]?


###### Exodus 17:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/17:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/17:3)


וַיִּצְמָ֨א שָׁ֤ם הָעָם֙ לַמַּ֔יִם וַיָּ֥לֶן הָעָ֖ם עַל־מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לָ֤מָּה זֶּה֙ הֶעֱלִיתָ֣נוּ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם לְהָמִ֥ית אֹתִ֛י וְאֶת־בָּנַ֥י וְאֶת־מִקְנַ֖י בַּצָּמָֽא׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the people thirsted there for water; and the people murmured against Moshe, and said, Why is it that thou hast brought us up out of Miżrayim, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst?


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the people thirsted there for water, and the people caviled against Moses, and said: Why did you bring us up from Egypt to put to death me, my children, and my cattle by thirst?


###### Exodus 17:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/17:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/17:4)


וַיִּצְעַ֤ק מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־יְהֹוָ֣ה לֵאמֹ֔ר מָ֥ה אֶעֱשֶׂ֖ה לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה ע֥וֹד מְעַ֖ט וּסְקָלֻֽנִי׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Moshe cried out to Adonoy saying, “What shall I do for this people? Before long they will stone me.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And Moshe cried to the Lord, saying, What shall I do to this people? they are almost ready to stone me.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

###### Exodus 17:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/17:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/17:5)


וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהֹוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה עֲבֹר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם וְקַ֥ח אִתְּךָ֖ מִזִּקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּמַטְּךָ֗ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִכִּ֤יתָ בּוֹ֙ אֶת־הַיְאֹ֔ר קַ֥ח בְּיָדְךָ֖ וְהָלָֽכְתָּ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Adonoy said to Moshe, “Pass to the front of the people and take with you the elders of the [B’nei] Yisrael. The staff with which you struck the river; take in to your hand, and go.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the Lord said to Moshe, Pass before the people, and take with thee of the elders of Yisra᾽el; and thy rod, with which thou smotest the river, take in thy hand, and go.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

And your staff wherewith you smote the Nile take in your hand and go [that it not be said that it is a "punishment staff" (having been used against Pharaoh and Egypt, and that it cannot effect good)].


###### Exodus 17:6

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**

**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock in Ḥorev; and thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it, that the people may drink. And Moshe did so in the sight of the elders of Yisra᾽el.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Behold, I shall stand before you there on the rock in Chorev, and you shall strike in the rock [into it, the staff being of hard sapphire] and water will come out of it and the people will drink. And Moses did thus before the eyes of the elders of Israel.

And Moses said to Joshua: Choose for us [you and me (whence it is derived that the honor of one's disciple should be as dear to one as his own)] men [warriors and fearers of sin, whose merits will avail them] and go out [of the cloud] and do battle with Amalek. Tomorrow I shall stand upon the top of the hill with the staff of G-d in my hand.

###### Exodus 17:12

וִידֵ֤י מֹשֶׁה֙ כְּבֵדִ֔ים וַיִּקְחוּ־אֶ֛בֶן וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ תַחְתָּ֖יו וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב עָלֶ֑יהָ וְאַהֲרֹ֨ן וְח֜וּר תָּֽמְכ֣וּ בְיָדָ֗יו מִזֶּ֤ה אֶחָד֙ וּמִזֶּ֣ה אֶחָ֔ד וַיְהִ֥י יָדָ֛יו אֱמוּנָ֖ה עַד־בֹּ֥א הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Moshe’s hands became heavy. They took a stone and placed it under him and he sat upon it. Aharon and Chur supported his hands, one of them on one side and one on the other side. His hands remained an expression of faith [as he prayed] until sunset.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
But Moshe’s hands were heavy; and they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat on it; and Aharon and Ḥur supported his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the hands of Moses became heavy [because he was lax in the mitzvah and deputed it to another (Joshua)], and they [Aaron and Chur] took a stone [(but not a pillow)] and placed it beneath him [(Moses associating himself with Israel's suffering)], and he sat on it. And Aaron and Chur supported his hands — one on one side, one on the other. And he was [i.e., he persisted with] his hands [spread out in an attitude of] steadfastness [in prayer] until the sun set. [The Amalekites would determine "propitious hours" for victory astrologically, and Moses caused the sun to stand still, thus confounding their reckonings.]

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And he said: For [the] hand [of the L-rd is raised to swear] by the throne [kes (as opposed to the complete form, kissei)] of Kah (the L-rd) [(as opposed to the complete name, Yod-Keh-Vav-Keh)]: "The L-rd is at war with Amalek from generation to generation" [The import: G-d's name will not be complete and His throne will not be complete until the name of Amalek is blotted out.]

**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
When Yitro, the priest of Midyan, Moshe’s father in law, heard 
				

				
				 of all that God had done for Moshe, and for Yisra᾽el his people, and that the Lord had brought Yisra᾽el out of Miżrayim;


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And Yithro heard [(of the splitting of the Red Sea and the war with Amalek and he came to join Israel)], the chief of Midian, the father-in-law of Moses [(Yithro now priding himself in Moses, whereas previously the reverse was the case (see 4:18)], all that G-d had done [(the falling of the manna, the welling of the water, the defeat of Amalek)] with Moses and with Israel, His people [(Moses being equated with all of Israel)] — that the L-rd had taken Israel out of Egypt [(this being the greatest of all)].

## Chapter 21

###### Exodus 21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:1)


וְאֵ֙לֶּה֙ הַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּשִׂ֖ים לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
And these are the laws that you shall set before them.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Now these are the judgments which thou shalt set before them.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And these [(Just as what precedes was stated at Sinai, so these)] are the judgments [(this section being juxtaposed with that of the altar to teach that the Sanhedrin should preside near the sanctuary)] that you should set [(as a "set" table, the judgments not merely to be mandated to them, but to be "digested" for them)] before them [and not before gentiles, even if their law, in the instance in question, coincides with Jewish law (this, to avoid diminution of the honor of Heaven)].


###### Exodus 21:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:2)

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If you buy a Hebrew slave, he shall serve [you] for six years, but in the seventh [year] he is to go out free, for naught [without liability].


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If thou buy a Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve: and in the seventh he shall go out free, for nothing.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If you buy [from beth-din] a Hebrew man-servant, six years shall he serve, and in the seventh he shall go out to freedom, gratis.


###### Exodus 21:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:3)


אִם־בְּגַפּ֥וֹ יָבֹ֖א בְּגַפּ֣וֹ יֵצֵ֑א אִם־בַּ֤עַל אִשָּׁה֙ ה֔וּא וְיָצְאָ֥ה אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ עִמּֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If he came by himself [unmarried], he shall go out by himself. If he was married, his wife shall go out with him.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If alone [without a wife] he came, alone shall he go out [(If he were not married when he came, his master may not give him a Canaanite bondswoman for the begetting of slaves)]. If he were the husband of a [Jewish] woman, then his wife shall go out with him. [(When did she come in?) It is hereby derived that one who buys a Hebrew man-servant is required to feed his wife and children.]


###### Exodus 21:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:4)

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If his master should give him a wife, and she bears him sons or daughters, then the woman and her children belong to her master, and he shall go out by himself.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If his master has given him a wife, and she has born him sons or daughters; the wife and her children shall be her master’s, and he shall go out by himself.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If his master gives him a woman [a Canaanite bondswoman], and she bears him sons or daughters, then the woman and her children shall belong to her master, and he shall go out alone.


###### Exodus 21:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:5)


וְאִם־אָמֹ֤ר יֹאמַר֙ הָעֶ֔בֶד אָהַ֙בְתִּי֙ אֶת־אֲדֹנִ֔י אֶת־אִשְׁתִּ֖י וְאֶת־בָּנָ֑י לֹ֥א אֵצֵ֖א חׇפְשִֽׁי׃

If the slave explicitly says, “I have come to love my master, my wife and my children, I do not want to go out free.”


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if the man-servant will say: I love my master, my wife [the bondswoman] and my children; I shall not go out free,


###### Exodus 21:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:6)


וְהִגִּישׁ֤וֹ אֲדֹנָיו֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְהִגִּישׁוֹ֙ אֶל־הַדֶּ֔לֶת א֖וֹ אֶל־הַמְּזוּזָ֑ה וְרָצַ֨ע אֲדֹנָ֤יו אֶת־אׇזְנוֹ֙ בַּמַּרְצֵ֔עַ וַעֲבָד֖וֹ לְעֹלָֽם׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
His master must bring him to the judges. He must then bring him next to the door, or to the doorpost, and his master shall pierce his ear with an awl. He then serves his master forever.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
then his master shall bring him to the judges; he shall also bring him to the door, or to the door post; and his master shall bore his ear through with an awl; and he shall serve him for ever.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
then his master shall bring him near to the judges [(The man-servant must consult the judges who sold him)], and he shall bring him near to the door or to the door-post [(Just as a door-post stands (in its place), so the door (against which his ear is bored) must be standing)], and his master shall bore his [right] ear with an awl, and he shall serve him forever [i.e., until the Jubilee year]. [Why the ear? The ear which heard on Mount Sinai: "Thou shalt not steal!" and he went and stole (for which reason beth-din sold him) — let his ear be bored! Or, if he sold himself: The ear which heard on Mount Sinai: "For unto Me are the children of Israel servants" and he went and acquired a master for himself — let his ear be bored! And why door and door-post? The Holy One Blessed be He said: The door and the door-post, which were witnesses in Egypt when I skipped over the lintel and the two door-posts (on which the Jews had sprinkled the blood of the Paschal lamb), and I said: "For unto Me are the children of Israel servants" — and not servants to servants (i.e., the Egyptians) and this one went and acquired a master for himself! Let his ear (that heard and did not listen) be bored (in their presence!)]


###### Exodus 21:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:7)


וְכִֽי־יִמְכֹּ֥ר אִ֛ישׁ אֶת־בִּתּ֖וֹ לְאָמָ֑ה לֹ֥א תֵצֵ֖א כְּצֵ֥את הָעֲבָדִֽים׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If a man sells his daughter to be a maidservant, she shall not go out [free] in the manner of male slaves.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And if a man sell his daughter to be a maidservant, she shall not go out as the menservants do.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if a man sells his daughter [a minor (under twelve)] as a maid, she shall not go out as the [Canaanite] bondsmen go out, [with the master's knocking out a tooth or an eye (but: at the end of six years, at the Jubilee year, or at her bringing (pubertal) signs — whichever is first)].


###### Exodus 21:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:8)


אִם־רָעָ֞ה בְּעֵינֵ֧י אֲדֹנֶ֛יהָ אֲשֶׁר־[ל֥וֹ] (לא) יְעָדָ֖הּ וְהֶפְדָּ֑הּ לְעַ֥ם נׇכְרִ֛י לֹא־יִמְשֹׁ֥ל לְמׇכְרָ֖הּ בְּבִגְדוֹ־בָֽהּ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If she is displeasing to her master, who had not designated her as his wife, he must allow her to be redeemed. He has no power [right] to sell her to an alien people for he has dealt deceitfully with her.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If she please not her master, who has designated her for himself, then shall he let her be redeemed: to sell her to a strange nation he shall have no power, seeing he has dealt deceitfully with her.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If she be ill-favored in the eyes of her master, who [on that account] did not designate her [to be his wife, even though he should have], then he shall [help] redeem her [by deducting from her six-year redemption money the value of the service she had already rendered]. To a strange nation [i.e., to another man] he [both the master and the father] shall not presume to sell her, after he [the master, by not taking her to wife, or the father, by selling her] has been faithless to her.

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If he takes himself another [wife], her sustenance, her clothing and her conjugal rights he must not diminish.

If he does not do these three things to her, she goes out free with no repayment of money.

Whoever curses his father or his mother shall be put to death.

And he that curses his father, or his mother, shall surely be put to death.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
When men quarrel and one man hits his fellow with a stone or with [his] fist; and he [the victim] does not die but becomes bedridden,


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

###### Exodus 21:19

If a man strikes his male or female slave with a rod, and [the slave] dies under his hand, [the death] must be avenged.

And if a man strike the eye of his [Canaanite] man-servant or the eye of his maid-servant, and he destroy it, free shall he send him in lieu of his eye [or any other organ prominences which do not grow back (excluding a child's tooth)].


###### Exodus 21:27

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:27](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:27)

If [he knocks out] the tooth of his slave, or knocks out the tooth of his female slave, he shall set him [the slave] free as compensation for the tooth.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:28](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:28)

See 29)]


###### Exodus 21:29

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:29](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/21:29)

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
When an atonement fine shall be imposed on him, he must give for the redemption of his soul whatever sum is imposed on him.

If there be laid on him a sum of money, then he shall give for the ransom of his life whatever is laid upon him.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
When kofer ["atonement" (payment)] is set for him, he shall give the redemption of his soul [(According to one view, the value of the victim; according to another, the value of the owner)], according to all that shall be set for him.


###### Exodus 21:31

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Whether it is a son [a minor lad] that is gored or a daughter [a minor girl] that it gored, this law shall apply to it.

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

If a man uncovers a pit, or if a man digs a pit, and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it;

If a man’s ox injures his neighbor’s ox and it dies, they shall sell the live ox and divide the money received for it. They shall also divide [the value of] the dead animal.

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If it was known that it was a goring ox from yesterday and the day before, but he had not taken proper precaution to guard it, then he must pay full compensation, an ox for an ox. The dead [animal] remains in the possession [of its owner].

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If a man steals an ox or a sheep, and then slaughters or sells it, he must pay five oxen for each ox, and four sheep for each sheep.

If the sun shone upon him [i.e., If it is obvious that the thief would not kill him (as in the instance of a father stealing from a son)], he (the thief) "has blood" [i.e., he is regarded as a "live man," and one who kills him is a murderer.] Pay shall he [the thief] pay [for what he stole (but he is not to be put to death)]. If he lacks it, he is to be sold for his theft.
