אִם־טָרֹ֥ף יִטָּרֵ֖ף יְבִאֵ֣הוּ עֵ֑ד הַטְּרֵפָ֖ה לֹ֥א יְשַׁלֵּֽם׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If it was torn apart [killed by wild beasts], he [the watcher] must provide witnesses. He then need not pay for that which was torn apart.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If it be torn in pieces, then let him bring it as evidence; he shall not make good that which was torn.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If it were torn [by a wild beast], let him bring witnesses [to that effect and thereby free himself of liability]. For the torn (beast) [(which he could not save, as when it was torn by a lion)] he shall not pay.


###### Exodus 22:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:13)


וְכִֽי־יִשְׁאַ֥ל אִ֛ישׁ מֵעִ֥ם רֵעֵ֖הוּ וְנִשְׁבַּ֣ר אוֹ־מֵ֑ת בְּעָלָ֥יו אֵין־עִמּ֖וֹ שַׁלֵּ֥ם יְשַׁלֵּֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If a man borrows something from his neighbor, and it becomes broken or dies; if the owner is not [involved] with him, he [the borrower] must make full restitution.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And if a man borrow aught of his neighbour, and it be hurt, or die, its owner not being with it, he shall surely make it good.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if a man borrow from his neighbor and it be broken or die, its owner not being with (i.e., engaged by) him [the borrower, in his work], pay shall he (the borrower) pay.


###### Exodus 22:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:14)


אִם־בְּעָלָ֥יו עִמּ֖וֹ לֹ֣א יְשַׁלֵּ֑ם אִם־שָׂכִ֣יר ה֔וּא בָּ֖א בִּשְׂכָרֽוֹ׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If the owner is [involved] with him, then he [the borrower] need not make restitution. If it was hired, it [the ox] comes in its rental price.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
But if its owner be with it, he shall not make it good: if it be a hired thing, it came for his hire.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If its owner were with him [whether in the same work (as the animal) or some other work, even if he were not with him at the time of breaking or death], he (the borrower) shall not pay. If it (the animal) were hired, it came by its hire [into the hands of the hirer, who, paying for it, (unlike the borrower), is not liable for mischance. (There is a difference of opinion as to whether he is to be regarded as an unpaid watcher or as a paid one.)]


###### Exodus 22:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:15)


וְכִֽי־יְפַתֶּ֣ה אִ֗ישׁ בְּתוּלָ֛ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־אֹרָ֖שָׂה וְשָׁכַ֣ב עִמָּ֑הּ מָהֹ֛ר יִמְהָרֶ֥נָּה לּ֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If a man seduces a virgin who is not betrothed, and lies with her; he must give the dowry to acquire her as his wife.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And if a man seduce a virgin that is not betrothed, and lie with her, he shall pay the bride price for her to be his wife.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And if a man entice a virgin who is not betrothed and he lie with her, he shall endower her unto himself as a wife [i.e., he shall write her a kethubah (a marriage contract) and marry her.]


###### Exodus 22:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:16)


אִם־מָאֵ֧ן יְמָאֵ֛ן אָבִ֖יהָ לְתִתָּ֣הּ ל֑וֹ כֶּ֣סֶף יִשְׁקֹ֔ל כְּמֹ֖הַר הַבְּתוּלֹֽת׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If her father utterly refuses to give her to him, he must give [the father] the weight of silver equal to the dowry usually given to virgins.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If her father utterly refuse to give her to him, he shall pay money according to the marriage price of virgins.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If her father refuse to give her to him, money shall he pay [fifty shekels] as per the indemnity for the [ravished] virgins (see Deuteronomy 22:29)].


###### Exodus 22:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:17)


מְכַשֵּׁפָ֖ה לֹ֥א תְחַיֶּֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You shall not allow a witch to live.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
A witch you shall not allow to live, [but you shall kill her, or him, as the case may be, (in beth-din)].


###### Exodus 22:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:18)


כׇּל־שֹׁכֵ֥ב עִם־בְּהֵמָ֖ה מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Whoever lies with an animal must be put to death.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Whoever cohabits with a beast shall surely be put to death.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Anyone who lies with a beast [either actively or passively] shall be put to death [by stoning].


###### Exodus 22:19

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:19](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:19)


זֹבֵ֥חַ לָאֱלֹהִ֖ים יׇֽחֳרָ֑ם בִּלְתִּ֥י לַיהֹוָ֖ה לְבַדּֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Whoever slaughters to a god must be condemned [to die]. [Sacrifices may be offered] to Adonoy alone.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
He that sacrifices to any god, save to the Lord only, he shall be utterly destroyed.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
One who slaughters [(or performs any inner Temple service, like slaughtering) to idolatry shall be put to death — only to the L-rd alone!


###### Exodus 22:20

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:20](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:20)


וְגֵ֥ר לֹא־תוֹנֶ֖ה וְלֹ֣א תִלְחָצֶ֑נּוּ כִּֽי־גֵרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You must not abuse or oppress a stranger, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thou shalt neither vex a stranger, nor oppress him: for you were strangers in the land of Miżrayim.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And a stranger [from another land] you shall not taunt and you shall not oppress him [by theft], for you were strangers in the land of Egypt [and are equally vulnerable to taunting].


###### Exodus 22:21

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:21](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:21)


כׇּל־אַלְמָנָ֥ה וְיָת֖וֹם לֹ֥א תְעַנּֽוּן׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You must not mistreat any widow or orphan.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
You shall not afflict any widow, or fatherless child.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Every widow and orphan you shall not afflict. [All men are intended; it is just that "widow and orphan" are more vulnerable to affliction.]


###### Exodus 22:22

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:22](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:22)


אִם־עַנֵּ֥ה תְעַנֶּ֖ה אֹת֑וֹ כִּ֣י אִם־צָעֹ֤ק יִצְעַק֙ אֵלַ֔י שָׁמֹ֥עַ אֶשְׁמַ֖ע צַעֲקָתֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If you do mistreat him [them], when he cries out to Me, I will indeed hear his cry.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If thou at all afflict them, and they cry to me, I will surely hear their cry;


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If you afflict him, [you will receive your just deserts]; for if he but cry out to Me, I will hear his cry.


###### Exodus 22:23

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:23](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:23)


וְחָרָ֣ה אַפִּ֔י וְהָרַגְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם בֶּחָ֑רֶב וְהָי֤וּ נְשֵׁיכֶם֙ אַלְמָנ֔וֹת וּבְנֵיכֶ֖ם יְתֹמִֽים׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Then I will cause My anger to flare, and I will kill you by the sword. Your wives will become widows and your children will be orphans.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and my anger shall be inflamed, and I will kill you with the sword; then your wives shall be widows, and your children fatherless.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And My wrath shall burn and I shall kill you by the sword, and your wives will be widows, and your children, orphans [There will be no witnesses to your death, and your wives will not be able to remarry or your sons to inherit you.]


###### Exodus 22:24

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:24](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:24)


אִם־כֶּ֣סֶף**׀** תַּלְוֶ֣ה אֶת־עַמִּ֗י אֶת־הֶֽעָנִי֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ לֹא־תִהְיֶ֥ה ל֖וֹ כְּנֹשֶׁ֑ה לֹֽא־תְשִׂימ֥וּן עָלָ֖יו נֶֽשֶׁךְ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
When you lend money to My people, to the poor person who is with [among] you, do not act toward him as a [demanding] creditor. Do not place the burden of interest upon him.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as a creditor, neither shall you lay upon him interest.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
When you lend money, [lend it, preferentially, in this order:] My people [before heathens], the poor man [before the relatively wealthier] with you [in your city, before the poor of other cities]. Do not be to him as a creditor [Do not be severe in demanding payment. If you know that he is without means, act towards him as if you had not lent him.] Do not impose interest (neshech) upon him, [neshech — "biting." Interest is like the biting of a snake. It begins with an almost imperceptible wound and then "swells" up to one's head.]


###### Exodus 22:25

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:25](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:25)


אִם־חָבֹ֥ל תַּחְבֹּ֖ל שַׂלְמַ֣ת רֵעֶ֑ךָ עַד־בֹּ֥א הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ תְּשִׁיבֶ֥נּוּ לֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If you take your neighbor’s garment as security, you must return it to him till sunset;


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If thou at all take thy neighbour’s garment for a pledge, thou shalt deliver it to him by sundown:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If you take as a pledge the garment of your neighbor [after the time for repayment of the loan arrives and he does not pay], until the setting of the sun return it to him. [Scripture here speaks of a day garment, which is not needed at night. (Restore it for the day and you may take it again at night.)]


###### Exodus 22:26

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:26](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:26)


כִּ֣י הִ֤וא כְסוּתֹה֙ לְבַדָּ֔הּ הִ֥וא שִׂמְלָת֖וֹ לְעֹר֑וֹ בַּמֶּ֣ה יִשְׁכָּ֔ב וְהָיָה֙ כִּֽי־יִצְעַ֣ק אֵלַ֔י וְשָׁמַעְתִּ֖י כִּֽי־חַנּ֥וּן אָֽנִי׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
For this alone is his covering, the garment [to cover] his skin. With what shall he lie down [to sleep]? If it happens that he cries out to Me, I will hear [his cry] for I am gracious.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
for that is his only covering, it is his garment for his skin: in what shall he sleep? and it shall come to pass, when he cries to me, that I will hear; for I am gracious.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For it is his solitary covering, [his outer garment]; it is his shirt for his skin [his inner garment]. On what shall he lie? [This includes his couch (as having to be returned for the day.)] And it shall be, if he cries out to Me, I shall hear; for I am gracious.


###### Exodus 22:27

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:27](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:27)


אֱלֹהִ֖ים לֹ֣א תְקַלֵּ֑ל וְנָשִׂ֥יא בְעַמְּךָ֖ לֹ֥א תָאֹֽר׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Do not curse judges. Do not curse a leader of your people.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thou shalt not revile the judges, nor curse the ruler of thy people.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Elohim you shall not curse [(an exhortation against cursing G-d and against cursing a judge)], and a prince in your people you shall not curse.


###### Exodus 22:28

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:28](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:28)


מְלֵאָתְךָ֥ וְדִמְעֲךָ֖ לֹ֣א תְאַחֵ֑ר בְּכ֥וֹר בָּנֶ֖יךָ תִּתֶּן־לִֽי׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
[Your offering of] the fullness [of your newly ripened produce] and of your terumah-offering’s you must not delay. The first-born of your sons, you shall give to Me.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thou shalt not delay to offer the first of thy ripe fruits, and of thy liquors: the firstborn of thy sons shalt thou give to me.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Your fullness [the obligation that is incumbent upon you when your produce has fully ripened, i.e., bikkurim (first fruits)] and your dema (terumah) you shall not delay [you are not to change the order of their separation. You are not to take terumah before bikkurim or ma'aser before terumah]. The first-born of your sons you shall give to Me [(Redeem him from the Cohein for five sela'im)].


###### Exodus 22:29

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:29](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:29)


כֵּֽן־תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה לְשֹׁרְךָ֖ לְצֹאנֶ֑ךָ שִׁבְעַ֤ת יָמִים֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה עִם־אִמּ֔וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁמִינִ֖י תִּתְּנוֹ־לִֽי׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You must do likewise with your oxen and with your sheep. Seven days it shall remain with its mother. On the eighth day you must give it to Me.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
In like manner shalt thou do with thy oxen, and with thy sheep: seven days it shall be with his dam; on the eighth day thou shalt give it me.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Thus shall you do with your ox, with your sheep [i.e., Just as a human bechor is redeemed after thirty days, so the bechor of small cattle (e.g., sheep) is to be looked after for thirty days and then given to the Cohein.] Seven days shall it be with its mother [(an exhortation to the Cohein not to sacrifice it before the eighth day)]; on the eighth day you may give it to Me.


###### Exodus 22:30

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:30](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/22:30)


וְאַנְשֵׁי־קֹ֖דֶשׁ תִּהְי֣וּן לִ֑י וּבָשָׂ֨ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֤ה טְרֵפָה֙ לֹ֣א תֹאכֵ֔לוּ לַכֶּ֖לֶב תַּשְׁלִכ֥וּן אֹתֽוֹ׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You shall be men of holiness to Me, and you must not eat flesh that was torn off in the field. Throw it to the dog.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And you shall be holy men to me: neither shall you eat any meat that is torn of beasts in the field; you shall cast it to the dogs.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And [if] men of holiness [i.e., If you separate yourselves from abominations of neveilah and treifah], you shall be unto Me [i.e., you shall be Mine; if not, you shall not be Mine.] And flesh torn [by a predatory animal from a live clean animal] in the field [(not necessarily the field, "the field" being the common instance)] you shall not eat; to the dog you shall throw it [or you may sell it to a heathen ("the dog" being mentioned to indicate that it takes precedence to selling and also that "the Holy One Blessed be He does not withhold the reward of any creature" (see 11:7)].



## Chapter 23

###### Exodus 23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:1)


לֹ֥א תִשָּׂ֖א שֵׁ֣מַע שָׁ֑וְא אַל־תָּ֤שֶׁת יָֽדְךָ֙ עִם־רָשָׁ֔ע לִהְיֹ֖ת עֵ֥ד חָמָֽס׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Do not accept a false report. Do not join hands with a wicked man to be a corrupt [false] witness.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thou shalt not raise a false report: put not thy hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Do not bear a false report [(an exhortation against receiving slander and an exhortation to a judge not to hear the words of one litigant before the other arrives)]. Do not place your hand with an evildoer [who puts forth a false claim against his neighbor] to [promise him to] be a false witness [for him].


###### Exodus 23:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:2)


לֹֽא־תִהְיֶ֥ה אַחֲרֵֽי־רַבִּ֖ים לְרָעֹ֑ת וְלֹא־תַעֲנֶ֣ה עַל־רִ֗ב לִנְטֹ֛ת אַחֲרֵ֥י רַבִּ֖ים לְהַטֹּֽת׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Do not follow the majority to do evil. Do not respond with your opinion in a dispute [merely] to lean [toward one side]. It must be decided by the majority.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil; neither shalt thou speak in a cause to incline after a multitude to pervert justice:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Do not incline [in judgment] after many [wicked men, simply because they are many] for evil. And do not answer [the defendant, who solicits your judgment] in the dispute, to incline after [those] many [wicked ones] to incline [the judgment from the truth; but judge in accordance with the truth and "let the collar (of responsibility) hang on the neck of the many"].


###### Exodus 23:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:3)


וְדָ֕ל לֹ֥א תֶהְדַּ֖ר בְּרִיבֽוֹ׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Do not show favor [even] to the poor in his dispute.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
nor shalt thou favour a poor man in his cause.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And do not honor a poor man in his quarrel [to favor him in judgment simply because he is poor].


###### Exodus 23:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:4)


כִּ֣י תִפְגַּ֞ע שׁ֧וֹר אֹֽיִבְךָ֛ א֥וֹ חֲמֹר֖וֹ תֹּעֶ֑ה הָשֵׁ֥ב תְּשִׁיבֶ֖נּוּ לֽוֹ׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If you come across your enemy’s ox or his donkey going astray, bring it back to him.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If thou meet thy enemy’s ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
If you encounter the ox of your foe, or his ass, straying, return shall you return it to him.


###### Exodus 23:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:5)


כִּֽי־תִרְאֶ֞ה חֲמ֣וֹר שֹׂנַאֲךָ֗ רֹבֵץ֙ תַּ֣חַת מַשָּׂא֔וֹ וְחָדַלְתָּ֖ מֵעֲזֹ֣ב ל֑וֹ עָזֹ֥ב תַּעֲזֹ֖ב עִמּֽוֹ׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
If you see the donkey of your enemy lying under its burden, and you might not want to help him, [but you should] make every effort to help him.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
If thou see the ass of him that hates thee lying under its burden, and wouldst forbear to unload it, thou shalt surely unload it with him.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Would you see the ass of your foe lying under its burden and forbear to help [disburden] it? Help shall you help [unload it] with him [the owner].


###### Exodus 23:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:6)


לֹ֥א תַטֶּ֛ה מִשְׁפַּ֥ט אֶבְיֹנְךָ֖ בְּרִיבֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Do not bend justice [even] for your needy in his dispute.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thou shalt not pervert the judgment of thy poor in his cause.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Do not incline the judgment of your needy one in his quarrel.


###### Exodus 23:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:7)


מִדְּבַר־שֶׁ֖קֶר תִּרְחָ֑ק וְנָקִ֤י וְצַדִּיק֙ אַֽל־תַּהֲרֹ֔ג כִּ֥י לֹא־אַצְדִּ֖יק רָשָֽׁע׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Keep far away from anything false. Do not kill an innocent righteous man, for I will not acquit a wicked person.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Keep thee far from a false matter; and the innocent and righteous slay thou not: for I will not justify the wicked.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
From a thing of falsehood keep far, and a clean one and a righteous one you shall not kill [("a clean one": If you have something to say in his favor after he has been sentenced to death, the case is to be reopened. "a righteous one": If you have something to say against him after he has been acquitted (i.e., found "righteous") the case is not to be re-opened)], for I will not find the wicked one righteous [(so that even if he has been erroneously acquitted, "the L-rd has many messengers")].


###### Exodus 23:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:8)


וְשֹׁ֖חַד לֹ֣א תִקָּ֑ח כִּ֤י הַשֹּׁ֙חַד֙ יְעַוֵּ֣ר פִּקְחִ֔ים וִֽיסַלֵּ֖ף דִּבְרֵ֥י צַדִּיקִֽים׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Do not accept bribery, for bribery blinds the clear-sighted, and perverts the words of justice.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt take no bribe: for the bribe blinds the wise, and perverts the words of the righteous.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And a bribe you shall not take [even to judge truly], for a bribe blinds the wise and undermines righteous words [i.e., true judgments].


###### Exodus 23:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:9)


וְגֵ֖ר לֹ֣א תִלְחָ֑ץ וְאַתֶּ֗ם יְדַעְתֶּם֙ אֶת־נֶ֣פֶשׁ הַגֵּ֔ר כִּֽי־גֵרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Do not oppress a stranger. You [should] know the soul [feelings] of the stranger, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Also thou shalt not oppress a stranger: for you know the heart of a stranger, seeing you were strangers in the land of Miżrayim.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And a stranger you shall not oppress. And you have known the soul of the stranger [how he suffers under oppression], for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.


###### Exodus 23:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:10)


וְשֵׁ֥שׁ שָׁנִ֖ים תִּזְרַ֣ע אֶת־אַרְצֶ֑ךָ וְאָסַפְתָּ֖ אֶת־תְּבוּאָתָֽהּ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You may sow your land for six years, and gather its crops.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And six years thou shalt sow thy land, and shalt gather in its fruits:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And six years shall you sow your land and you shall gather [into your house] its produce.


###### Exodus 23:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:11)


וְהַשְּׁבִיעִ֞ת תִּשְׁמְטֶ֣נָּה וּנְטַשְׁתָּ֗הּ וְאָֽכְלוּ֙ אֶבְיֹנֵ֣י עַמֶּ֔ךָ וְיִתְרָ֕ם תֹּאכַ֖ל חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה כֵּֽן־תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה לְכַרְמְךָ֖ לְזֵיתֶֽךָ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
But on the seventh [year] you must let it rest, and abandon it [by not eating its produce], and let the needy among your people eat it. What they leave over, the beasts of the field can eat. Do the same with your vineyard and your olive [trees].


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
but the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie fallow; that the poor of thy people may eat: and what they leave, the beasts of the field shall eat. In like manner thou shalt deal with thy vineyard, and with thy olive grove.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the seventh year it shall lie fallow [and not be worked] and you shall leave it [i.e., you shall not eat of its produce after the time of removal (see Leviticus 25:7)], and the poor of your people shall eat it, and what they leave shall be eaten by the animals of the field [(Just as it need not be tithed for animals, so it need not be tithed for the poor — whence it is derived that ma'aser does not obtain in the sabbatical year)]. Thus shall you [also] do with your vineyard and with your olive grove, [(what precedes applying to a grain field)].


###### Exodus 23:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:12)


שֵׁ֤שֶׁת יָמִים֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה מַעֲשֶׂ֔יךָ וּבַיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖י תִּשְׁבֹּ֑ת לְמַ֣עַן יָנ֗וּחַ שֽׁוֹרְךָ֙ וַחֲמֹרֶ֔ךָ וְיִנָּפֵ֥שׁ בֶּן־אֲמָתְךָ֖ וְהַגֵּֽר׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You may do your work six days, but on the seventh day you must cease; so that your ox and your donkey may rest, and the son of your female slave may be refreshed, and [also] the stranger.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Six days thou shalt do thy work, and on the seventh day thou shalt rest: that thy ox and thy ass may rest; and the son of thy handmaid, and the stranger, may be refreshed.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Six days shall you do your work, and on the seventh day shall you rest [i.e., Shabbath is not superseded by Shevi'ith (which is also a commemoration of the creation)], so that there rest your ox and your ass [Give it "resting," i.e., allow it to tear grass from the earth and eat it], and there be refreshed the son of your maidservant [an uncircumcised Canaanite servant] and the stranger [a ger toshav, a "sojourning stranger" (one who shuns idolatry and observes the seven Noachide laws)].


###### Exodus 23:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:13)


וּבְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־אָמַ֥רְתִּי אֲלֵיכֶ֖ם תִּשָּׁמֵ֑רוּ וְשֵׁ֨ם אֱלֹהִ֤ים אֲחֵרִים֙ לֹ֣א תַזְכִּ֔ירוּ לֹ֥א יִשָּׁמַ֖ע עַל־פִּֽיךָ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Preserve everything that I have said to you. Do not mention the name of other gods. You must not cause it to be heard through your mouth.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And all things that I have said to you be mindful of: and make no mention of the name of other gods, neither let it be heard out of thy mouth.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And all that I have spoken to you, you shall observe [(all positive commandments are hereby "affixed" with an exhortation)]. And the name of other gods you shall not mention [One should not say to another: "Wait for me near that idol" (mentioning its name) or "Stand with me on the festival of that idol"]; it shall not be heard [from the gentile] upon your mouth [i.e., at your instigation. (Do not enter into partnership with a gentile, lest he swear by his god (in the instance of a dispute) in which instance you are an accessory to the mentioning of idolatry.)]

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:14)


שָׁלֹ֣שׁ רְגָלִ֔ים תָּחֹ֥ג לִ֖י בַּשָּׁנָֽה׃

Three times a year you are to celebrate with Me.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Three times shall you celebrate for Me in the year.


###### Exodus 23:15

אֶת־חַ֣ג הַמַּצּוֹת֮ תִּשְׁמֹר֒ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִים֩ תֹּאכַ֨ל מַצּ֜וֹת כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֗ךָ לְמוֹעֵד֙ חֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽאָבִ֔יב כִּי־ב֖וֹ יָצָ֣אתָ מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וְלֹא־יֵרָא֥וּ פָנַ֖י רֵיקָֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You must keep the festival of Matzos. You must eat matzos for seven days, as I have commanded you. [This festival must be celebrated] at the appointed time, during the month when the grain is ripened, for in it [at this time] you went out of Egypt. Do not appear before My Presence empty-handed.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thou shalt keep the feast of unleavened bread: (thou shalt eat unleavened bread seven days, as I commanded thee, in the time appointed of the month Aviv; for in it thou didst come out from Miżrayim: and none shall appear before me empty:)


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The festival of matzoth shall you keep. Seven days shall you eat matzoth, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of aviv, [when the grain begins to ripen]; for in it did you go out of Egypt. And they shall not appear before Me empty-handed, [but they shall bring burnt-offerings].


###### Exodus 23:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:16)


וְחַ֤ג הַקָּצִיר֙ בִּכּוּרֵ֣י מַעֲשֶׂ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּזְרַ֖ע בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה וְחַ֤ג הָֽאָסִף֙ בְּצֵ֣את הַשָּׁנָ֔ה בְּאׇסְפְּךָ֥ אֶֽת־מַעֲשֶׂ֖יךָ מִן־הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃

[You must also keep] the Festival of Harvest, [with bringing bikurim] the first fruits of your labor, which you planted in the field; [also] the Festival of Ingathering, at the close of the year, when you gather in [the fruits of] your labor from the field.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and the feast of harvest, the firstfruits of thy labours, which thou hast sown in the field: and the feast of ingathering, which is at the end of the year, when thou hast gathered in thy labours out of the field.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the festival of the harvest [Shavuoth], the [time of bringing the] first-fruits of your labor, which you sow in the field [(the two loaves of Shavuoth permitting the new wheat for meal-offerings and the bringing of first-fruits to the Temple, viz. (Numbers 28:26)], and the festival of the ingathering [Succoth] at the going out of the year, when you gather your labor from the field [against the rain].


###### Exodus 23:17

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Three times a year, every male among you must appear before the Presence of the Master, Adonoy.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Three times in the year all thy males shall appear before the Lord God.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Three times in the year shall appear all the males among you in the presence of the Master, the L-rd, [the festivals not lapsing in the sabbatical year].

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:18)


לֹֽא־תִזְבַּ֥ח עַל־חָמֵ֖ץ דַּם־זִבְחִ֑י וְלֹֽא־יָלִ֥ין חֵֽלֶב־חַגִּ֖י עַד־בֹּֽקֶר׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You must not sacrifice—while chometz is present—My [Pesach] sacrifice. You must not allow to remain overnight—the fat of My festival-offering—until morning.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread; neither shall the fat of my sacrifice remain until the morning.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
You shall not offer alongside chametz the blood of My sacrifice [i.e., Do not slaughter the Pesach offering on the fourteenth of Nissan until the chametz has been removed], and there shall not remain [unplaced on the altar] the fat of My festival offering until morning.


###### Exodus 23:19

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:19](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:19)


רֵאשִׁ֗ית בִּכּוּרֵי֙ אַדְמָ֣תְךָ֔ תָּבִ֕יא בֵּ֖ית יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ לֹֽא־תְבַשֵּׁ֥ל גְּדִ֖י בַּחֲלֵ֥ב אִמּֽוֹ׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The beginning of the first fruits of your land must be brought to the House of Adonoy, your God. You must not cook a young animal in the milk of its mother.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The first of the firstfruits of thy land thou shalt bring to the house of the Lord thy God. Thou shalt not boil a kid in its mother’s milk.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The first of the first-fruits of your land [even in the sabbatical year] you shall bring to the house of the L-rd your G-d. You shall not cook a kid [any young, tender animal] in its mother's milk. [This is written three times in the Torah: (here, 34:26, and Deuteronomy 14:21), once to forbid eating (milk and meat together), once to forbid derivation of benefit, and once to forbid cooking.]


###### Exodus 23:20

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:20](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:20)


הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י שֹׁלֵ֤חַ מַלְאָךְ֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ לִשְׁמׇרְךָ֖ בַּדָּ֑רֶךְ וְלַהֲבִ֣יאֲךָ֔ אֶל־הַמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֲכִנֹֽתִי׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Behold, I will send an angel before you, to guard you on the way, and to bring you to the place that I have prepared.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Behold, I send an angel before thee, to keep thee in the way, and to bring thee to the place which I have prepared.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Behold, I shall send an angel before you [(the L-rd here apprising them that they would sin, that He would not go up among them (33:3) and that they would require an intermediary)], to watch over you on the way, and to bring you to the place that I have readied [for you].


###### Exodus 23:21

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:21](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:21)


הִשָּׁ֧מֶר מִפָּנָ֛יו וּשְׁמַ֥ע בְּקֹל֖וֹ אַל־תַּמֵּ֣ר בּ֑וֹ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יִשָּׂא֙ לְפִשְׁעֲכֶ֔ם כִּ֥י שְׁמִ֖י בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Be careful in his presence and heed [obey] his voice. Do not rebel against him; for he cannot bear [pardon] your transgression, as My Name is in him.

Take heed of him, and obey his voice, provoke him not; for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Take heed of him and hearken to his voice. Do not rebel against him, for he will not forgive your offenses, [sin being foreign to his nature and forgiveness not being deputed to him. "Take heed of him"] for My name is within him [i.e., associated with him].

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:22](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:22)


כִּ֣י אִם־שָׁמ֤וֹעַ תִּשְׁמַע֙ בְּקֹל֔וֹ וְעָשִׂ֕יתָ כֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲדַבֵּ֑ר וְאָֽיַבְתִּי֙ אֶת־אֹ֣יְבֶ֔יךָ וְצַרְתִּ֖י אֶת־צֹרְרֶֽיךָ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
But if you truly listen to [obey] his voice, and do all that I speak, then I will be an enemy to your enemies, and attack those who attack you.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
But if thou shalt indeed obey his voice, and do all that I speak; then I will be an enemy to thy enemies, and an adversary to thy adversaries.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
But if you hearken to his voice and do all that I shall speak, then I shall hate your enemies and oppress your oppressors.


###### Exodus 23:23

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:23](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:23)


כִּֽי־יֵלֵ֣ךְ מַלְאָכִי֮ לְפָנֶ֒יךָ֒ וֶהֱבִֽיאֲךָ֗ אֶל־הָֽאֱמֹרִי֙ וְהַ֣חִתִּ֔י וְהַפְּרִזִּי֙ וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י הַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִ֑י וְהִכְחַדְתִּֽיו׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
My messenger will go before you, and will bring you into [the land of] the Emorites, the Chittites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, Chivites, and the Yevusites, and I will then annihilate them.

For my angel shall go before thee, and bring thee in to the Emori, and the Ḥitti, and the Perizzi, and the Kena῾ani, and the Ḥivvi, and the Yevusi; and I will cut them off.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
For My angel shall go before you, and he will bring you to the Emori, and the Chitti and the Perizi and the Canaani and the Chivi and the Yevussi, and I will annihilate them.


###### Exodus 23:24

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:24](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/23:24)


לֹֽא־תִשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֤ה לֵאלֹֽהֵיהֶם֙ וְלֹ֣א תׇֽעׇבְדֵ֔ם וְלֹ֥א תַעֲשֶׂ֖ה כְּמַֽעֲשֵׂיהֶ֑ם כִּ֤י הָרֵס֙ תְּהָ֣רְסֵ֔ם וְשַׁבֵּ֥ר תְּשַׁבֵּ֖ר מַצֵּבֹתֵיהֶֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You must not prostrate yourself to their gods, nor serve [sacrifice to] them. You must not adopt their customs. You must totally destroy [their idols] and completely break down their monuments.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Do not bow down to their gods and do not worship them and do not emulate their deeds, but raze them [their idols] and break down their [stone] monuments [which they set up to bow down to].

("him"): "And the glory of the L-rd reposed upon Mount Sinai and the cloud covered him for six days [after the Ten Commandments, the beginning of the forty days of Moses' going up to receive the tablets (Scripture teaching that entrance into the "Divine Encampment" (later, the Holy of Holies) requires a six-day separation period)], and He called to Moses on the seventh day from the midst of the cloud."]

Adonoy spoke to Moshe saying,

**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**

**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Speak to the B’nei Yisrael and have them take for Me a terumah-offering. From every man whose heart impels him to generosity shall you take My terumah-offering.

[Three terumoth are referred to here: the terumah of a beka for a head, of which the sockets were made; the terumah of the altar, a beka for a head, for the communal offering funds; and the terumah of the mishkan (the tabernacle), an individual gift. (The thirteen articles mentioned below were needed either for the work of the mishkan or for the priestly garments)].

And there shall be a bulb under two branches of the same piece, and a bulb under two branches of the same piece, and a bulb under two branches of the same piece, according to the six branches that proceed out of the candlestick.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And a bulb under the two branches from it [the one piece of gold], and a bulb under the (next) two branches from it, and a bulb under the (next) two branches from it, (thus) for (all) the six branches that project from the menorah.


###### Exodus 25:36

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/25:36](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/25:36)


כַּפְתֹּרֵיהֶ֥ם וּקְנֹתָ֖ם מִמֶּ֣נָּה יִהְי֑וּ כֻּלָּ֛הּ מִקְשָׁ֥ה אַחַ֖ת זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Their knobs and their branches shall be made out of [the menorah] itself. It shall all be made of a single hammered work of pure gold.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Their bulbs and their branches shall be made of the same piece: all shall be one beaten work of pure gold.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Their bulbs and their branches from it shall be, all one (piece of) beaten work of pure gold.


###### Exodus 25:37

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/25:37](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/25:37)


וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת־נֵרֹתֶ֖יהָ שִׁבְעָ֑ה וְהֶֽעֱלָה֙ אֶת־נֵ֣רֹתֶ֔יהָ וְהֵאִ֖יר עַל־עֵ֥בֶר פָּנֶֽיהָ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You shall make seven lamps [for the menorah]. and its lamps shall be lit so that they shine toward it [the center lamp].


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt make its seven lamps: and they shall light its lamps, that they may give light over against it.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall make its lamps [small bowls into which oil and wicks were placed], seven, and he (the artificer) shall fashion its lamps so that their light is directed at its face [the central shaft].


###### Exodus 25:38

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/25:38](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/25:38)


וּמַלְקָחֶ֥יהָ וּמַחְתֹּתֶ֖יהָ זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Its tongs and its [ash] scoops [shall also be made of] pure gold.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And its tongs, and its ashpans, shall be of pure gold.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And its tongs [for manipulating and positioning the wicks] and its snuff-dishes [small bowls into which the high-priest raked the ashes every morning], pure gold.


###### Exodus 25:39

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/25:39](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/25:39)


כִּכָּ֛ר זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹתָ֑הּ אֵ֥ת כׇּל־הַכֵּלִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
It shall be made out of a kikar of pure gold [together] with all these vessels.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Of a talent of pure gold shall he make it, with all these vessels.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
(Of) a talent of pure gold shall he make it [together] with all these vessels.


###### Exodus 25:40

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/25:40](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/25:40)


וּרְאֵ֖ה וַעֲשֵׂ֑ה בְּתַ֨בְנִיתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֥ה מׇרְאֶ֖ה בָּהָֽר׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Observe [carefully] and make them like the pattern that will be shown to you on the mountain.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And look that thou make them after their pattern, which was shown thee in the mountain.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And see, and make (them) according to their design which you are shown [here] in the mountain.



## Chapter 26

###### Exodus 26:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:1)


וְאֶת־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֥ן תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה עֶ֣שֶׂר יְרִיעֹ֑ת שֵׁ֣שׁ מׇשְׁזָ֗ר וּתְכֵ֤לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָן֙ וְתֹלַ֣עַת שָׁנִ֔י כְּרֻבִ֛ים מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה חֹשֵׁ֖ב תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You shall [then] make the mishkon (Tabernacle) out of ten drapes, [consisting of] fine twined linen, greenish blue, dark red and crimson [wool]. Figures of cherubim, the work of a craftsman, shall be woven into them.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Moreover thou shalt make the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet: with keruvim of artistic work shalt thou make them.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the tabernacle (the *mishkan*) shall you make with ten curtains [to serve it as a roof and as partitions outside the boards, the curtains being hung behind them to cover them]: twisted linen (*shesh*) and blue (wool) and purple and scarlet, [four varieties in each thread, one of linen and three of wool and each thread twisted six (*shesh*) times, giving a twenty-four-fold thread], cherubs of artistic work [(figures interwoven on both sides)] shall you make them.


###### Exodus 26:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:2)


אֹ֣רֶךְ**׀** הַיְרִיעָ֣ה הָֽאַחַ֗ת שְׁמֹנֶ֤ה וְעֶשְׂרִים֙ בָּֽאַמָּ֔ה וְרֹ֙חַב֙ אַרְבַּ֣ע בָּאַמָּ֔ה הַיְרִיעָ֖ה הָאֶחָ֑ת מִדָּ֥ה אַחַ֖ת לְכׇל־הַיְרִיעֹֽת׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Each drape shall be twenty eight amohs long, and each drape shall be four amohs wide. All the drapes shall have the same measure.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The length of one curtain shall be twenty eight cubits, and the breadth of one curtain four cubits: and the curtains shall be all of one measure.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The length of one curtain, twenty-eight cubits; and the width, four cubits for one curtain — one measure for all the curtains.


###### Exodus 26:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:3)


חֲמֵ֣שׁ הַיְרִיעֹ֗ת תִּֽהְיֶ֙יןָ֙ חֹֽבְרֹ֔ת אִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל־אֲחֹתָ֑הּ וְחָמֵ֤שׁ יְרִיעֹת֙ חֹֽבְרֹ֔ת אִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל־אֲחֹתָֽהּ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Five of these drapes shall be joined [sewn] together and [the other] five drapes shall be joined [sewn] together.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The five curtains shall be coupled together one to another; and the other five curtains shall be coupled one to another.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Five curtains shall be attached [by sewing] one to the other, and five curtains, one to the other.


###### Exodus 26:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:4)


וְעָשִׂ֜יתָ לֻֽלְאֹ֣ת תְּכֵ֗לֶת עַ֣ל שְׂפַ֤ת הַיְרִיעָה֙ הָאֶחָ֔ת מִקָּצָ֖ה בַּחֹבָ֑רֶת וְכֵ֤ן תַּעֲשֶׂה֙ בִּשְׂפַ֣ת הַיְרִיעָ֔ה הַקִּ֣יצוֹנָ֔ה בַּמַּחְבֶּ֖רֶת הַשֵּׁנִֽית׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Make loops of greenish blue [wool] on the edge of the drape which is at the [innermost] end of the [first] group. Do the same on the edge of the drape which is at the [innermost] end of the second group.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt make loops of blue upon the edge of the one curtain that is at the edge of the first coupling; and likewise shalt thou make in the uttermost edge of the curtain, that is outmost in the second coupling.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall make loops of purple wool at the edge of the end curtain of one (five-curtain) joining, and, likewise, at the edge of the end curtain of the other joining.


###### Exodus 26:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:5)


חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים לֻֽלָאֹ֗ת תַּעֲשֶׂה֮ בַּיְרִיעָ֣ה הָאֶחָת֒ וַחֲמִשִּׁ֣ים לֻֽלָאֹ֗ת תַּעֲשֶׂה֙ בִּקְצֵ֣ה הַיְרִיעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בַּמַּחְבֶּ֣רֶת הַשֵּׁנִ֑ית מַקְבִּילֹת֙ הַלֻּ֣לָאֹ֔ת אִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל־אֲחֹתָֽהּ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Make fifty loops on [the edge of] one drape, and make fifty loops on the edge of the drape which is on the second group. The loops shall be opposite one another.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Fifty loops shalt thou make in the one curtain, and fifty loops shalt thou make in the edge of the curtain that is in the second coupling; that the loops may take hold one of another.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Fifty loops shall you make in the one (end) curtain, and fifty loops shall you make at the edge of the (end) curtain in the second joining, the loops [on the respective joinings] directly aligned one with the other.


###### Exodus 26:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:6)


וְעָשִׂ֕יתָ חֲמִשִּׁ֖ים קַרְסֵ֣י זָהָ֑ב וְחִבַּרְתָּ֨ אֶת־הַיְרִיעֹ֜ת אִשָּׁ֤ה אֶל־אֲחֹתָהּ֙ בַּקְּרָסִ֔ים וְהָיָ֥ה הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן אֶחָֽד׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Make fifty golden clasps, and join the drapes [of each group] together with the clasps, so that the mishkon is one.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt make fifty golden clasps, and couple the curtains together with the clasps: that the tabernacle may be one.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall make fifty golden hooks, and you shall join the curtains one to the other by the hooks, [inserting one end of the hook into one loop, and the other end, into its corresponding loop], and the tabernacle shall be one.


###### Exodus 26:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:7)


וְעָשִׂ֙יתָ֙ יְרִיעֹ֣ת עִזִּ֔ים לְאֹ֖הֶל עַל־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן עַשְׁתֵּי־עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה יְרִיעֹ֖ת תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Make drapes of goats hair for a covering over the mishkon. Make eleven drapes.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt make curtains of goats’ hair to be a covering upon the tabernacle: eleven curtains shalt thou make.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall make curtains of goats' hair to tent over the [lower curtains of the] tabernacle; eleven curtains shall you make them.


###### Exodus 26:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:8)


אֹ֣רֶךְ**׀** הַיְרִיעָ֣ה הָֽאַחַ֗ת שְׁלֹשִׁים֙ בָּֽאַמָּ֔ה וְרֹ֙חַב֙ אַרְבַּ֣ע בָּאַמָּ֔ה הַיְרִיעָ֖ה הָאֶחָ֑ת מִדָּ֣ה אַחַ֔ת לְעַשְׁתֵּ֥י עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה יְרִיעֹֽת׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The length of each drape shall be thirty amohs, and the width of each drape shall be four amohs. The eleven drapes must have the same measure.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
The length of one curtain shall be thirty cubits, and the breadth of one curtain four cubits: and the eleven curtains shall be all of one measure.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
The length of one curtain, thirty cubits; and the width, four cubits for one curtain — one measure for the eleven curtains.


###### Exodus 26:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:9)


וְחִבַּרְתָּ֞ אֶת־חֲמֵ֤שׁ הַיְרִיעֹת֙ לְבָ֔ד וְאֶת־שֵׁ֥שׁ הַיְרִיעֹ֖ת לְבָ֑ד וְכָפַלְתָּ֙ אֶת־הַיְרִיעָ֣ה הַשִּׁשִּׁ֔ית אֶל־מ֖וּל פְּנֵ֥י הָאֹֽהֶל׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Join [sew] together five drapes by themselves, and [the other] six drapes by themselves. Let the sixth drape overhang before the entrance of the tent [mishkon].


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt couple five curtains by themselves, and six curtains by themselves, and shalt double the sixth curtain in the forefront of the tabernacle.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall join five curtains separately and six curtains separately, and you shall double [two cubits of] the sixth curtain [the "surplus" vis-à-vis the lower curtains] over the face of the tent [the screen on the east (as a bride's face is veiled in modesty)].


###### Exodus 26:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:10)


וְעָשִׂ֜יתָ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים לֻֽלָאֹ֗ת עַ֣ל שְׂפַ֤ת הַיְרִיעָה֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ת הַקִּיצֹנָ֖ה בַּחֹבָ֑רֶת וַחֲמִשִּׁ֣ים לֻֽלָאֹ֗ת עַ֚ל שְׂפַ֣ת הַיְרִיעָ֔ה הַחֹבֶ֖רֶת הַשֵּׁנִֽית׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Make fifty loops on the edge of one drape which is at the [innermost] end of the [first] group, and fifty loops on the edge of the drape which is on the second group.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt make fifty loops on the edge of the one curtain that is outmost in the coupling, and fifty loops in the edge of the curtain of the second coupling.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall make fifty loops at the edge of the end curtain in (one) joining, and fifty loops at the edge of the curtain in the second joining.


###### Exodus 26:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:11)


וְעָשִׂ֛יתָ קַרְסֵ֥י נְחֹ֖שֶׁת חֲמִשִּׁ֑ים וְהֵבֵאתָ֤ אֶת־הַקְּרָסִים֙ בַּלֻּ֣לָאֹ֔ת וְחִבַּרְתָּ֥ אֶת־הָאֹ֖הֶל וְהָיָ֥ה אֶחָֽד׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Make fifty copper clasps. Bring the clasps into the loops, and join the tent together, making it one.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt make fifty clasps of brass, and put the clasps into the loops, and couple the tent together, that it may be one.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall make fifty copper hooks, and you shall insert the hooks into the loops, and you shall join the tent [the goats' hair covering], and it shall be one.


###### Exodus 26:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:12)


וְסֶ֙רַח֙ הָעֹדֵ֔ף בִּירִיעֹ֖ת הָאֹ֑הֶל חֲצִ֤י הַיְרִיעָה֙ הָעֹדֶ֔פֶת תִּסְרַ֕ח עַ֖ל אֲחֹרֵ֥י הַמִּשְׁכָּֽן׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The overlapping excess [from what is left over] [in the breadth] of the drapes of the tent—half of the extra drape shall overlap the back of the mishkon.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the remnant that remains of the curtains of the tent, the half curtain that remains, shall hang over the back of the tabernacle.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the additional draping in the curtains of the tent, half of the additional curtain [i.e., two cubits], you shall hang over the back [the west] of the tabernacle [to cover the two cubits of exposed beams.]


###### Exodus 26:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:13)


וְהָאַמָּ֨ה מִזֶּ֜ה וְהָאַמָּ֤ה מִזֶּה֙ בָּעֹדֵ֔ף בְּאֹ֖רֶךְ יְרִיעֹ֣ת הָאֹ֑הֶל יִהְיֶ֨ה סָר֜וּחַ עַל־צִדֵּ֧י הַמִּשְׁכָּ֛ן מִזֶּ֥ה וּמִזֶּ֖ה לְכַסֹּתֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The [extra] amoh on one side, and the [extra] amoh on the other side that were in excess of the length of the drapes of the tent shall overlap the sides of the mishkon, on both sides, to cover it.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And a cubit on the one side, and a cubit on the other side, of that which remains in the length of the curtains of the tent, shall hang over the sides of the tabernacle on this side and on that side, to cover it.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the cubit on one side and the cubit on the other side in excess [of the length of the lower curtains] in the length of the curtains of the tent, shall be spread over both sides [north and south] of the tabernacle [curtains] to cover it [(for purposes of adornment)].


###### Exodus 26:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:14)


וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ מִכְסֶה֙ לָאֹ֔הֶל עֹרֹ֥ת אֵילִ֖ם מְאׇדָּמִ֑ים וּמִכְסֵ֛ה עֹרֹ֥ת תְּחָשִׁ֖ים מִלְמָֽעְלָה׃{פ}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Make a covering for the tent out of red dyed ram’s skins, and a covering of tachash skins above that.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt make a covering for the Tent, of rams’ skins dyed red, and a covering above of taĥash skins.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall make a cover for the tent [(the goats' hair roof)] of rams' skins dyed red, and a cover of tachash skins above.


###### Exodus 26:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:15)


וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת־הַקְּרָשִׁ֖ים לַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן עֲצֵ֥י שִׁטִּ֖ים עֹמְדִֽים׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Make the planks for the mishkon out of acacia wood; [these planks are] to stand upright [vertically].


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt make boards for the tabernacle of shittim wood standing up.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall make the beams of the tabernacle [those that have been designated for the purpose (Jacob, prophetically, having planted acacia trees to this end)] of standing acacia wood. [The beams of the tabernacle walls are to be stood up vertically, and not placed horizontally one atop the other.]


###### Exodus 26:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:16)


עֶ֥שֶׂר אַמּ֖וֹת אֹ֣רֶךְ הַקָּ֑רֶשׁ וְאַמָּה֙ וַחֲצִ֣י הָֽאַמָּ֔ה רֹ֖חַב הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Each plank shall be ten amohs long, and one and one half amohs shall be the width of each plank.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Ten cubits shall be the length of a board, and a cubit and a half shall be the breadth of one board.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Ten cubits the length of the beam [(so that the height of the tabernacle was ten cubits)], and a cubit and a half the breadth of each beam [(so that the length of the tabernacle was thirty cubits)].


###### Exodus 26:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:17)


שְׁתֵּ֣י יָד֗וֹת לַקֶּ֙רֶשׁ֙ הָאֶחָ֔ד מְשֻׁ֨לָּבֹ֔ת אִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל־אֲחֹתָ֑הּ כֵּ֣ן תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל קַרְשֵׁ֥י הַמִּשְׁכָּֽן׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Each plank shall have two [square] pegs, exactly parallel to each other. So shall you make all the planks of the mishkon.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Two tenons shall there be in one board, connected one with the other: thus shalt thou make for all the boards of the tabernacle.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
Two prongs (wooden projections) for each beam [(the beam being hollowed out at the bottom to form these prongs)], rung-like, one near the other [like the rungs of a ladder]. So shall you do for all the beams of the tabernacle.


###### Exodus 26:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:18)


וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת־הַקְּרָשִׁ֖ים לַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן עֶשְׂרִ֣ים קֶ֔רֶשׁ לִפְאַ֖ת נֶ֥גְבָּה תֵימָֽנָה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Make these planks for the mishkon, twenty planks for the southern side.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt make the boards for the tabernacle, twenty boards on the south side southward.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall make the beams for the tabernacle, twenty beams for the southern side.


###### Exodus 26:19

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:19](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:19)


וְאַרְבָּעִים֙ אַדְנֵי־כֶ֔סֶף תַּעֲשֶׂ֕ה תַּ֖חַת עֶשְׂרִ֣ים הַקָּ֑רֶשׁ שְׁנֵ֨י אֲדָנִ֜ים תַּֽחַת־הַקֶּ֤רֶשׁ הָאֶחָד֙ לִשְׁתֵּ֣י יְדֹתָ֔יו וּשְׁנֵ֧י אֲדָנִ֛ים תַּֽחַת־הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָ֖ד לִשְׁתֵּ֥י יְדֹתָֽיו׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Make forty silver sockets, [and place them] under the twenty planks. There shall be two sockets under one plank [one] for each of the two pegs, and two sockets under the other plank, [one] for each of the two pegs.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt make forty sockets of silver under the twenty boards; two sockets under one board for its two tenons, and two sockets under another board for its two tenons.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And forty silver sockets shall you make under the twenty beams; two sockets under one beam for its two prongs, and two sockets under the next beam for its two prongs.


###### Exodus 26:20

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:20](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:20)


וּלְצֶ֧לַע הַמִּשְׁכָּ֛ן הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית לִפְאַ֣ת צָפ֑וֹן עֶשְׂרִ֖ים קָֽרֶשׁ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
For the second wall of the mishkon, to the northern side, [also make] twenty planks.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And for the second side of the tabernacle on the north side there shall be twenty boards:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And for the second side of the tabernacle, the northern side, twenty beams.


###### Exodus 26:21

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:21](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:21)


וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים אַדְנֵיהֶ֖ם כָּ֑סֶף שְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֗ים תַּ֚חַת הַקֶּ֣רֶשׁ הָֽאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
[Make] their forty silver sockets, two sockets under each plank, two sockets under each plank.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and their forty sockets of silver: two sockets under one board, and two sockets under another board.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And their forty silver sockets, two sockets under one beam and two sockets under the next beam.


###### Exodus 26:22

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:22](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:22)


וּֽלְיַרְכְּתֵ֥י הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן יָ֑מָּה תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה שִׁשָּׁ֥ה קְרָשִֽׁים׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
For the west end of the mishkon make six planks.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And for the side of the tabernacle westward thou shalt make six boards.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And for the ends [i.e., the back] of the tabernacle on the west, you shall make six beams, [accounting for nine cubits of width.]


###### Exodus 26:23

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:23](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:23)


וּשְׁנֵ֤י קְרָשִׁים֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה לִמְקֻצְעֹ֖ת הַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן בַּיַּרְכָתָֽיִם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Make two planks for the corners of the mishkon at the rear side.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And two boards shalt thou make for the corners of the tabernacle in the west side.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And two beams shall you make for the corners of the tabernacle at the ends, [(so that the interior width is ten cubits)].


###### Exodus 26:24

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:24](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:24)


וְיִֽהְי֣וּ תֹֽאֲמִם֮ מִלְּמַ֒טָּה֒ וְיַחְדָּ֗ו יִהְי֤וּ תַמִּים֙ עַל־רֹאשׁ֔וֹ אֶל־הַטַּבַּ֖עַת הָאֶחָ֑ת כֵּ֚ן יִהְיֶ֣ה לִשְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם לִשְׁנֵ֥י הַמִּקְצֹעֹ֖ת יִהְיֽוּ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
They must be coupled together on the bottom, and they must also be coupled together evenly on the top with one [square] ring. So must it be done with the two [planks], which are at the two corners.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And they shall be coupled together beneath, and they shall be coupled together above the head of it unto one ring: thus shall it be for them both; they shall be for the two corners.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And they (the beams) shall be fitted against each other at the bottom, and together shall they be fitted at its top into one ring. [Two adjacent beams were fixed together by a ring placed in grooves along their breadth.] So shall it be for the two of them [for the two beams at the end, the beam at the northern end and the western beam, and so,] for the two corners shall they be.


###### Exodus 26:25

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:25](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:25)


וְהָיוּ֙ שְׁמֹנָ֣ה קְרָשִׁ֔ים וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֣ם כֶּ֔סֶף שִׁשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר אֲדָנִ֑ים שְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֗ים תַּ֚חַת הַקֶּ֣רֶשׁ הָאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Thus there will be eight planks, and their silver sockets, totaling sixteen sockets, two sockets under each plank, two sockets under each plank.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And they shall be eight boards, and their sockets of silver, sixteen sockets; two sockets under one board, and two sockets under another board.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And [on the western side] there shall be eight beams and their silver sockets, sixteen sockets; two sockets under one beam and two sockets under the next beam.


###### Exodus 26:26

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:26](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:26)


וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ בְרִיחִ֖ם עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים חֲמִשָּׁ֕ה לְקַרְשֵׁ֥י צֶֽלַע־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן הָאֶחָֽד׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You shall make bars out of acacia wood, five for the planks of one wall,


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt make bars of shittim wood; five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall make bars of acacia wood, five for the beams of one side of the tabernacle [These "five" are three, the upper and lower bars, respectively, consisting of two equal (fifteen cubit segments) running along the side wall, and one bar running the entire length through a hole bored in each beam.]


###### Exodus 26:27

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:27](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:27)


וַחֲמִשָּׁ֣ה בְרִיחִ֔ם לְקַרְשֵׁ֥י צֶֽלַע־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן הַשֵּׁנִ֑ית וַחֲמִשָּׁ֣ה בְרִיחִ֗ם לְקַרְשֵׁי֙ צֶ֣לַע הַמִּשְׁכָּ֔ן לַיַּרְכָתַ֖יִם יָֽמָּה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
and five bars for the planks of the second wall of the mishkon. [There shall also be] five bars for the planks of the western [back] wall of the mishkon.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and five bars for the boards of the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the third side of the tabernacle, for the side westward.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And five bars for the beams of the second side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the beams of the side of the tabernacle at the western ends.


###### Exodus 26:28

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:28](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:28)


וְהַבְּרִ֥יחַ הַתִּיכֹ֖ן בְּת֣וֹךְ הַקְּרָשִׁ֑ים מַבְרִ֕חַ מִן־הַקָּצֶ֖ה אֶל־הַקָּצֶֽה׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
The middle [center] bar shall go through the planks, reinforcing the planks from one end to the other.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the middle bar in the midst of the boards shall reach from end to end.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the middle bar in the midst of the beams shall extend from end to end.


###### Exodus 26:29

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:29](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:29)


וְֽאֶת־הַקְּרָשִׁ֞ים תְּצַפֶּ֣ה זָהָ֗ב וְאֶת־טַבְּעֹֽתֵיהֶם֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה זָהָ֔ב בָּתִּ֖ים לַבְּרִיחִ֑ם וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֶת־הַבְּרִיחִ֖ם זָהָֽב׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You shall overlay the planks with gold, and make their rings out of gold, to hold the bars. You shall [also] overlay the bars with gold.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt overlay the boards with gold, and make their rings of gold as places for the bars: and thou shalt overlay the bars with gold.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And the beams shall you cover with gold, and their rings shall you make of gold [to serve as] housings for the bars, and you shall cover the bars with gold [i.e., They will be "covered" with gold when they are inserted into the golden rings flanked by the golden half-reeds on either side.]


###### Exodus 26:30

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:30](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:30)


וַהֲקֵמֹתָ֖ אֶת־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן כְּמִ֨שְׁפָּט֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הׇרְאֵ֖יתָ בָּהָֽר׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You shall erect the mishkon according to its rules. As shown to you on the mountain.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt rear up the tabernacle according to its fashion which was shown thee in the mountain.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall set up the tabernacle after the manner which will have been shown to you [by the L-rd] in the mountain.


###### Exodus 26:31

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:31](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:31)


וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ פָרֹ֗כֶת תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מׇשְׁזָ֑ר מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה חֹשֵׁ֛ב יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָ֖הּ כְּרֻבִֽים׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You shall make a paroches [partition] out of greenish blue wool, dark red wool, crimson wool, and twined, fine linen. It shall be the work of a craftsman, with figures of cherubim [woven into it].


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt make a veil of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen with keruvim shall it be made of artistic work:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall make a *parocheth* (partition) of blue wool and purple wool and scarlet wool and twisted linen. Artistic work shall he make it, cherubs. [See Rashi on verse 1].


###### Exodus 26:32

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:32](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:32)


וְנָתַתָּ֣ה אֹתָ֗הּ עַל־אַרְבָּעָה֙ עַמּוּדֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֔ים מְצֻפִּ֣ים זָהָ֔ב וָוֵיהֶ֖ם זָהָ֑ב עַל־אַרְבָּעָ֖ה אַדְנֵי־כָֽסֶף׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Place it [the paroches] upon four acacia-wood pillars, that are overlaid with gold. Their hooks shall [also] be of gold. These pillars are to be set into four silver sockets.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
and thou shalt hang it upon four pillars of shittim wood overlaid with gold: their hooks shall be of gold, upon four sockets of silver.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall place it on four pillars of acacia wood covered with gold, their hooks of gold [(Hooks bent upwards were set in the pillars on which to place the pole on which the top of the *parocheth* was wrapped)] (the pillars standing) upon four sockets of silver.


###### Exodus 26:33

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:33](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:33)


וְנָתַתָּ֣ה אֶת־הַפָּרֹ֘כֶת֮ תַּ֣חַת הַקְּרָסִים֒ וְהֵבֵאתָ֥ שָׁ֙מָּה֙ מִבֵּ֣ית לַפָּרֹ֔כֶת אֵ֖ת אֲר֣וֹן הָעֵד֑וּת וְהִבְדִּילָ֤ה הַפָּרֹ֙כֶת֙ לָכֶ֔ם בֵּ֣ין הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ וּבֵ֖ין קֹ֥דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Place the paroches under the clasps [which kept the drapes together]. Bring into the space within [behind] the paroches, the Ark of the Testimony, and the paroches will divide for you between the Holy and the Holy of Holies.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt hang up the veil under the clasps, that thou mayst bring in there within the veil the ark of the Testimony: and the veil shall be for you as a division between the holy place and the most holy.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall put the *parocheth* under the hooks, and you shall bring there, inside the *parocheth*, the ark of testimony; and the *parocheth* shall separate for you between the holy and the holy of holies.


###### Exodus 26:34

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:34](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:34)


וְנָתַתָּ֙ אֶת־הַכַּפֹּ֔רֶת עַ֖ל אֲר֣וֹן הָעֵדֻ֑ת בְּקֹ֖דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Place the cover upon the Ark of the Testimony in the Holy of Holies.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt put the covering upon the ark of the Testimony in the most holy place.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall put the *kaporeth* (the lid) upon the ark of testimony in the holy of holies.


###### Exodus 26:35

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:35](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:35)


וְשַׂמְתָּ֤ אֶת־הַשֻּׁלְחָן֙ מִח֣וּץ לַפָּרֹ֔כֶת וְאֶת־הַמְּנֹרָה֙ נֹ֣כַח הַשֻּׁלְחָ֔ן עַ֛ל צֶ֥לַע הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן תֵּימָ֑נָה וְהַ֨שֻּׁלְחָ֔ן תִּתֵּ֖ן עַל־צֶ֥לַע צָפֽוֹן׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Put the table outside the paroches, and the menorah opposite the table, toward the southern side of the mishkon. The table should be placed on the northern side.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt set the table outside the veil, and the candlestick over against the table on the side of the tabernacle toward the south: and thou shalt put the table on the north side.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall place the table outside the *parocheth*, and the menorah opposite the table on the southern side of the tabernacle; and the table shall you place on the northern side.


###### Exodus 26:36

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:36](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:36)


וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ מָסָךְ֙ לְפֶ֣תַח הָאֹ֔הֶל תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מׇשְׁזָ֑ר מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה רֹקֵֽם׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You shall make a screen for the entrance of the tent. [Make it out of] greenish blue wool, dark red wool, crimson wool, and twined, fine linen. It shall be the work of an embroiderer.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt make a screen for the door of the tent, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, the work of an embroiderer.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall make a screen [a curtain] for the entrance of the tent, of blue wool, purple wool, scarlet wool, and twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer [needlework, the figures on one side being the same as those on the other.]


###### Exodus 26:37

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:37](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/26:37)


וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לַמָּסָ֗ךְ חֲמִשָּׁה֙ עַמּוּדֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֔ים וְצִפִּיתָ֤ אֹתָם֙ זָהָ֔ב וָוֵיהֶ֖ם זָהָ֑ב וְיָצַקְתָּ֣ לָהֶ֔ם חֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אַדְנֵ֥י נְחֹֽשֶׁת׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Make five pillars of acacia wood for the screen. Overlay them with gold and their hooks are to be gold. Cast five copper sockets for them [the pillars].


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt make for the screen five pillars of shittim wood, and overlay them with gold, and their hooks shall be of gold: and thou shalt cast five sockets of brass for them.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall make for the screen five pillars of acacia wood, and you shall cover them with gold, and their hooks (shall be) of gold; and you shall cast for them five copper sockets.



## Chapter 27

###### Exodus 27:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/27:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/27:1)


וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים חָמֵשׁ֩ אַמּ֨וֹת אֹ֜רֶךְ וְחָמֵ֧שׁ אַמּ֣וֹת רֹ֗חַב רָב֤וּעַ יִהְיֶה֙ הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וְשָׁלֹ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת קֹמָתֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You shall make the altar out of acacia wood. It shall be five amohs long, and five amohs wide. The altar shall be square, and its height shall be three amohs.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt make an altar of shittim wood, five cubits long, and five cubits broad; the altar shall be foursquare: and the height of it shall be three cubits.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall make the altar of acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide. The altar shall be square and three cubits high.


###### Exodus 27:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/27:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/27:2)


וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ קַרְנֹתָ֗יו עַ֚ל אַרְבַּ֣ע פִּנֹּתָ֔יו מִמֶּ֖נּוּ תִּהְיֶ֣יןָ קַרְנֹתָ֑יו וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹת֖וֹ נְחֹֽשֶׁת׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Make its raised projections on its four corners. Its raised projections shall be of one piece with it, and you shall overlay it [the altar] with copper.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt make the horns of it upon its four corners: its horns shall be of the same: and thou shalt overlay it with brass.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall make its horns on its four corners. From it [the altar itself] shall its horns be, [and not first made and then attached to it.] and you shall cover it with copper [to atone for brazenness (see Isaiah 48:4)].


###### Exodus 27:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/27:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/27:3)


וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ סִּֽירֹתָיו֙ לְדַשְּׁנ֔וֹ וְיָעָיו֙ וּמִזְרְקֹתָ֔יו וּמִזְלְגֹתָ֖יו וּמַחְתֹּתָ֑יו לְכׇל־כֵּלָ֖יו תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה נְחֹֽשֶׁת׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Make its pots to remove its ashes, [also] its scoops, its basins, its flesh hooks, and its fire pans. Make all of its vessels out of copper.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt make its pans to receive its ashes, and its shovels, and its basins, and its forks, and its firepans: all its vessels thou shalt make of brass.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall make its pots (into which) to empty its ashes, and its shovels [with which to remove its ashes], and its sprinkling basins [in which to receive the blood of the sacrifices], and its spits, and its fire-pans [for taking coals from the outer altar to the inner altar for the burning of the incense]. All of its implements shall you make of copper.


###### Exodus 27:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/27:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/27:4)


וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ לּוֹ֙ מִכְבָּ֔ר מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה רֶ֣שֶׁת נְחֹ֑שֶׁת וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ עַל־הָרֶ֗שֶׁת אַרְבַּע֙ טַבְּעֹ֣ת נְחֹ֔שֶׁת עַ֖ל אַרְבַּ֥ע קְצוֹתָֽיו׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Make for it a grate of copper netting. On the grate you shall make four copper rings on its four corners.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt make for it a grate of network of brass; and upon the net shalt thou make four brazen rings on its four corners.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall make for it a copper lattice, netting work. And you shall make on the netting four copper rings at its four edges.


###### Exodus 27:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/27:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/27:5)


וְנָתַתָּ֣ה אֹתָ֗הּ תַּ֛חַת כַּרְכֹּ֥ב הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ מִלְּמָ֑טָּה וְהָיְתָ֣ה הָרֶ֔שֶׁת עַ֖ד חֲצִ֥י הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Place it under the rim of the altar, extending downward, so that the grate reaches the middle of the altar.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt put it under the ledge of the altar beneath, that the net may reach to the midst of the altar.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall place it under the karkov of the altar [an encircling, decorative band] below. And the netting shall extend until the mid-point of the altar [for distinguishing between the (placing of the) "upper blood" and the "lower blood"].


###### Exodus 27:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/27:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/27:6)


וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ בַדִּים֙ לַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ בַּדֵּ֖י עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹתָ֖ם נְחֹֽשֶׁת׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with copper.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And thou shalt make poles for the altar, poles of shittim wood, and overlay them with brass.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall make staves for the altar of acacia wood, and you shall cover them with copper.


###### Exodus 27:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/27:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/27:7)


וְהוּבָ֥א אֶת־בַּדָּ֖יו בַּטַּבָּעֹ֑ת וְהָי֣וּ הַבַּדִּ֗ים עַל־שְׁתֵּ֛י צַלְעֹ֥ת הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ בִּשְׂאֵ֥ת אֹתֽוֹ׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
Place its poles into the rings, and the poles shall be on the two sides of the altar when it is carried.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
And the poles shall be put into the rings, and the poles shall be upon the two sides of the altar, to carry it.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And its staves shall be brought into the [four] rings [made in the lattice]. And the staves shall be on the two sides of the altar when it is carried.


###### Exodus 27:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/27:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/27:8)


נְב֥וּב לֻחֹ֖ת תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹת֑וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר הֶרְאָ֥ה אֹתְךָ֛ בָּהָ֖ר כֵּ֥ן יַעֲשֽׂוּ׃{ס}


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
It should be a hollow structure constructed from boards. As it was shown to you on the mountain, so shall they make it.


**The Koren Jerusalem Bible:**
Hollow with boards shalt thou make it: as it was shown thee in the mountain, so shall they make it.


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
A hollow of boards shall you make it, as He showed you on the mountain; so shall they do.


###### Exodus 27:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/27:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Exodus/r/27:9)


וְעָשִׂ֕יתָ אֵ֖ת חֲצַ֣ר הַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן לִפְאַ֣ת נֶֽגֶב־תֵּ֠ימָ֠נָה קְלָעִ֨ים לֶחָצֵ֜ר שֵׁ֣שׁ מׇשְׁזָ֗ר מֵאָ֤ה בָֽאַמָּה֙ אֹ֔רֶךְ לַפֵּאָ֖ה הָאֶחָֽת׃


**Metsudah Chumash, Metsudah Publications, 2009:**
You shall make the enclosure for the mishkon. On the south side there shall be curtains for the enclosure made of fine twined linen. It shall be one hundred amohs long on one side.

And thou shalt make the court of the tabernacle: for the south side southward there shall be hangings for the court of fine twined linen of a hundred cubits long for one side:


**The Rashi chumash by Rabbi Shraga Silverstein:**
And you shall make the court of the tabernacle: On the south side, curtains for the court, of twisted linen, a hundred cubits long on one side.
